capacity-superpowers.title: Capacity — Developing SuperPowers
capacity-superpowers.subtitle: Developing SuperPowers
capacity-superpowers.tagline: Don’t wait for your Goliath to start developing your sling.
capacity-superpowers.bigIdea: Giants do not create capacity. Giants reveal capacity.
capacity-superpowers.openLine: Your SuperPower is not what you wish you could do. Your SuperPower is the capacity you have taken time to develop.
capacity-superpowers.closeLine: Don't wait for your Goliath to start developing your sling.

themeScripture.text: The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.

declaration: I will build in The Cave.
I will stand in The Covenant.
I will live for The Cause.
I will act with Courage.
I will produce Conquest.

weeks.title: Cave · Competence
weeks.ask: Where is God building competence in you right now?
weeks.rhyme:
In the cave where no one sees,
God is training hands and knees;
Lion, bear, and sling, and stone —
Competence is built alone!

weeks.title: Covenant · Confidence
weeks.ask: Where is God building confidence in you right now?
weeks.rhyme:
I am not my height or size,
Covenant has better eyes;
Whose I am is who I'll be —
Confidence lives inside me!

weeks.title: Cause · Conviction
weeks.ask: Where is God building conviction in you right now?
weeks.rhyme:
Is there not a cause? There is!
Bigger than my wants and wish;
Born to answer, not applaud —
Conviction takes its cause from God!

weeks.title: Courage
weeks.ask: Where is God building courage in you right now?
weeks.rhyme:
Not one stone stays in my hand,
I will run, I will not stand;
Move while shaking — take the shot!
Courage uses what I've got!

weeks.title: Conquest · Impact
weeks.ask: Where is God building impact in you right now?
weeks.rhyme:
Giant falls and armies rise,
Someone else believes and tries;
Not just blessed — I'm sent to be
God's own answer. Come and see!

1.title: Hidden Before Heard

scripture.text: And Samuel said unto Jesse, Are here all thy children? And he said, There remaineth yet the youngest, and, behold, he keepeth the sheep.

1.truth: Being left out is not being left behind.
1.hook: Somebody in this family is missing — and the prophet of God refuses to start until he arrives. Have you ever been the empty chair?

points.title: Being left out is not being left behind.
points.body: Seven sons were presented to a prophet and nobody sent for David. God stopped the entire ceremony until the forgotten one arrived.

points.title: Hidden is not the same as forgotten.
points.body: He was in a field, not in disgrace. God knew the address.

points.title: The anointing came before the crown.
points.body: Where you are is not who you are.

1.illustration: David was not even invited when Samuel came. Never despise hidden seasons.
1.challenge: Write your name on a card. Underneath, write one thing God has said about you that people cannot see yet. Keep it in your school bag all September.
1.declaration: I will develop privately until I can deliver publicly.
questions: What is in your heart today that only God can see — and are you glad He can see it? (1 Samuel 16:7)

mirrors.ot: Joseph — youngest, sold, forgotten in a pit and a prison, while God wrote “Prime Minister” over him (Genesis 37; 41:41).
mirrors.nt: “Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers” (1 Timothy 4:12).

1.christ: Jesus grew up in Nazareth — the town people asked, “Can any good thing come out of Nazareth?” (John 1:46); “he is despised and rejected of men” (Isaiah 53:3). If they overlooked the Saviour of the world, being overlooked cannot disqualify you.
1.code: Hidden is not the same as forgotten.

quiz.q: How many sons were presented to the prophet before David was sent for?
Where was David when the prophet came?
What did God do when the forgotten one had not yet arrived?
options: He sent Saul to fetch him

2.title: Faithful With Sheep

scripture.text: But David went and returned from Saul to feed his father's sheep at Bethlehem.

2.truth: Small things are the entrance exam.
2.hook: One of these is the reason you will ever get the other. Guess which one comes first.

points.title: He went back.
points.body: He had been in a palace and he still went back to the sheep. Competence does not get offended by small work.

points.title: “Those few sheep” was a real assignment.
points.body: Eliab later said it as an insult (17:28). God called it training.

points.title: Small things are the entrance exam.
points.body: “He chose David also his servant, and took him from the sheepfolds” (Psalm 78:70). Not around them. From them.

2.illustration: Before David managed a nation, he managed sheep. Your current assignment is training for your next one.
2.challenge: Pick the small duty at home you usually avoid. Do it today, unasked and unannounced.
questions: Name the “few sheep” God has given you this season. Have you been feeding them? (Luke 16:10)

mirrors.ot: Ruth gleaning in a corner of a field she did not own — and that ordinary field placed her in the family line of Christ (Ruth 2:2–3; Matthew 1:5).
mirrors.nt: “He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much” (Luke 16:10).

2.christ: Jesus spent about thirty years in a carpenter's shop and about three in public ministry — ten times more hidden faithfulness than public ministry. And He is “the good shepherd” who “giveth his life for the sheep” (John 10:11). He is not asking you to do anything He has not already done.
2.code: Small things are the entrance exam.

quiz.q: Where did David go back to after his time in Saul's presence?
How did Eliab use the words “those few sheep”?
According to the day, what are small things?

3.title: The Lion Lesson

scripture.text: And David said unto Saul, Thy servant kept his father's sheep, and there came a lion, and a bear, and took a lamb out of the flock:

3.truth: Every private battle you win, you win on His strength.
3.hook: Nobody clapped. Nobody filmed it. Nobody even knew. And it is the reason Goliath died.

points.title: The lion came for what he was carrying.
points.body: It took a lamb out of the flock. Attacks often target your assignment, not just you.

points.title: He went after it himself.
points.body: No report, no negotiation, no waiting for reinforcements. Competence deals with what is in front of it.

points.title: Nobody clapped.
points.body: There was no crowd, no camera, no prize. That is exactly why it counted.

3.illustration: David learned courage fighting what nobody celebrated. Small battles build big capacity.
3.challenge: Name one “lion” — a habit, a fear, a temptation that keeps stealing from you. Tell God about it tonight, by name.
questions: What has been taken from you that God wants you to go back and recover? (1 Peter 5:8–9)

mirrors.ot: Samson tore a lion in a vineyard with nobody watching (Judges 14:5–6) — a private victory before a public deliverance.
mirrors.nt: “Your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about... whom resist stedfast in the faith” (1 Peter 5:8–9).

3.christ: There is a Lion who fights for us — “the Lion of the tribe of Juda hath prevailed” (Revelation 5:5). David fought one; we belong to one. Every private battle you win, you win on His strength.
3.code: Competence deals with what is in front of it.

quiz.q: What did the lion take?
options: A lamb out of the flock

quiz.q: Who went after the lion?
What was true of the fight with the lion?
options: It was reported to the king

4.title: The Bear Lesson

scripture.text: And I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth:

4.truth: God repeats a lesson until the lesson is in you.
4.hook: Lion. Bear. Giant. God never sends the giant first.

points.title: God repeats a lesson until the lesson is in you.
points.body: The lion taught him. The bear proved he had learned.

points.title: He recovered what was taken.
points.body: “I went out after him, and smote him, and delivered it out of his mouth.” God builds recoverers, not just survivors.

points.title: The second one was bigger and he was not afraid.
points.body: That is the definition of growing capacity: the next thing is harder and it no longer frightens you.

4.illustration: One victory became preparation for another. Every challenge can become training.
4.challenge: Start your lion-and-bear page — write down one hard thing God has already brought you through. Add to it all month.
questions: What has God already delivered you from that you have stopped thanking Him for? (1 Samuel 17:37)

mirrors.ot: Moses given two signs at the burning bush — the rod and the hand — so the first would be believed (Exodus 4:1–9).
mirrors.nt: “Who delivered us from so great a death, and doth deliver: in whom we trust that he will yet deliver us” (2 Corinthians 1:10) — past, present, future, one God.

4.christ: Jesus was tested three times in the wilderness before He preached one sermon (Matthew 4:1–11), and returned “in the power of the Spirit” (Luke 4:14). Private test, then public power. Always that order.
4.code: God never sends the giant first.

quiz.q: How many animals had David fought before the giant?
What did David recover from the bear's mouth?
What is the lion-and-bear page for?
options: Recording hard things God has already brought you through

5.title: Practise Your Sling

scripture.text: And he took his staff in his hand, and chose him five smooth stones out of the brook, and put them in a shepherd's bag which he had, even in a scrip; and his sling was in his hand: and he drew near to the Philistine.

5.hook: Now imagine doing this ten thousand times before anybody is watching. That is the entire difference between David and me.

points.title: A sling is only a weapon in a practised hand.
points.body: In an untrained hand it is a piece of leather. The tool is not the SuperPower — the developed tool is.

points.title: Dependable beats impressive.
points.body: David's sling was not the most powerful weapon in that valley. It was the most reliable one he had.

points.title: You cannot practise during the fight.
points.body: Whatever you have not developed before the giant will not be available in front of the giant.

5.illustration: David's weapon worked because he had used it before. Develop your gift until it becomes dependable. Later, in the cave of Adullam (1 Samuel 22:1–2), four hundred men in distress, in debt and discontented came to David there, and that cave produced his mighty men.
5.challenge: Name one gift God has given you. Commit to practising it for fifteen minutes a day, every day, to the end of September.
questions: Which of your gifts have you never actually developed? (Hebrews 5:14)

mirrors.ot: “What is that in thine hand?” — a shepherd's rod, used daily for forty years, became the rod of God (Exodus 4:2).
mirrors.nt: “Strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised” (Hebrews 5:14). Use is what makes it strong.

5.christ: “Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered” (Hebrews 5:8) — so we have a High Priest “touched with the feeling of our infirmities” (Hebrews 4:15). Jesus was proved in real conditions so that He can help you in yours.

quiz.q: When is a sling only a piece of leather, according to the day?
What made David's sling work in that valley?
options: It was the most powerful weapon
It was the most reliable one he had

quiz.q: When can you not practise, according to the day?

7.title: Who Are You?

scripture.text: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee.

7.hook: Write who you are. Not your name — who you ARE.

points.title: You were made on purpose, with purpose.
points.body: “I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made” (Psalm 139:14). Nothing about you is an accident.

points.title: God knew you before anybody named you.
points.body: “Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee” (Jeremiah 1:5). Your identity is older than your birthday.

points.title: Capacity is discovered, not invented.
points.body: You are not trying to become somebody. You are learning what God already put in you.

7.challenge: Write three true sentences that begin “I am…” — using only what God's word says about you.
7.declaration: I know who I am, whose I am, and what God has put inside me.
questions: Do you believe you were made on purpose? What would change today if you did? (Psalm 139:14)

mirrors.ot: Gideon was hiding in a winepress when the angel called him “thou mighty man of valour” (Judges 6:12). God named him by his future, not his hiding place.
mirrors.nt: “We are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them” (Ephesians 2:10).

7.christ: Jesus knew exactly who He was — “I know whence I came, and whither I go” (John 8:14) — and He is the one who gives us our identity: “as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God” (John 1:12). You do not find yourself. You find Him, and He tells you who you are.

quiz.q: What did God know before anybody named you?
options: You, before you were formed in the belly

quiz.q: According to the day, how is capacity received?
Where was Gideon hiding when the angel named him?

8.title: Whose Are You?

scripture.text: Know ye that the LORD he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.

8.truth: You belong to God before you belong to any crowd.
8.hook: No name on it. No owner. So anybody can pick it up — and anybody can throw it away. Do you know who owns you?

points.title: He made us, not we ourselves.
points.body: “Know ye that the LORD he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.”

points.title: Belonging settles you.
points.body: A child who knows whose they are stops auditioning for every crowd.

points.title: Ownership means covering.
points.body: If you are His sheep, He is your shepherd — and shepherds fight lions.

8.illustration: You belong to God before you belong to any crowd.
8.challenge: Notice one moment today when you were tempted to change who you are to fit in. Choose differently.
questions: Whose approval have you been working hardest for this year? (Psalm 100:3)

mirrors.ot: “Fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine” (Isaiah 43:1).
mirrors.nt: “Ye are not your own... for ye are bought with a price” (1 Corinthians 6:19–20).

8.christ: “My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me... neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand” (John 10:27–28). The price of your belonging was His blood. That is how secure your identity is.
8.code: You belong to God before you belong to any crowd.

quiz.q: Who made us, according to the day's reading?
options: He made us, not we ourselves

quiz.q: What does belonging do for a child, according to the day?
options: It settles them and stops them auditioning for every crowd
It replaces the need for prayer

quiz.q: What do shepherds do, in the day's point about covering?

9.title: Uncircumcised Philistine

scripture.text: And David spake to the men that stood by him, saying, What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine, and taketh away the reproach from Israel? for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?

9.hook: “NINE FEET TALL.” “NO COVENANT.” Both of these are true about Goliath. One of them is about to get him killed. Which one?

points.title: David measured Goliath against God, not himself.
points.body: Against David, Goliath was huge. Against “the armies of the living God,” he was nothing.

points.title: Covenant is the real measurement.
points.body: His confidence was not in his size but in his side.

points.title: Naming things correctly disarms them.
points.body: Everyone else said “the champion.” David said “this uncircumcised Philistine” — a man with no covenant and therefore no covering.

9.challenge: Write your giant's name. Beside it write: “compared to the living God, you are ______.” Fill it in truthfully.
questions: Are you measuring your problem against yourself, or against God? (1 John 4:4)

mirrors.ot: Jonathan, two men against a garrison: “there is no restraint to the LORD to save by many or by few” (1 Samuel 14:6).
mirrors.nt: “Greater is he that is in you, than he that is in the world” (1 John 4:4).

9.christ: We are in a better covenant — “a surety of a better testament” (Hebrews 7:22) — sealed by Christ's own blood. At the cross He “spoiled principalities and powers... triumphing over them in it” (Colossians 2:15). Your giants are already-defeated enemies still making noise.

quiz.q: Against whom was Goliath huge?
options: Against the armies of the living God

quiz.q: Where was David's confidence, according to the day?
What did David call Goliath?

10.title: Don't Wear Saul's Armour

scripture.text: And Saul armed David with his armour, and he put an helmet of brass upon his head; also he armed him with a coat of mail.

10.hook: Somebody is dressing you like this right now. And you are saying thank you.

points.title: Saul dressed David like Saul.
points.body: “And Saul armed David with his armour.” People will always try to reproduce themselves in you.

points.title: What protects one person can paralyse another.
points.body: The armour was not bad. It was not his.

points.title: “I cannot go with these” is a complete sentence.
points.body: Said respectfully, to a king — and then he took it off. Confidence knows how to decline.

10.illustration: Don't lose yourself trying to become somebody else.
10.challenge: Name one thing you are only doing because somebody else does it. Take it off this week.
questions: Whose armour have you been wearing? (1 Corinthians 12:14)

mirrors.ot: Aaron's garments were made “for glory and for beauty” and fitted to specific men (Exodus 28:2–4). God has never done one-size-fits-all.
mirrors.nt: “There are diversities of gifts, but the same Spirit... the body is not one member, but many” (1 Corinthians 12:4, 14). Comparison is a category error.

10.christ: Jesus refused every costume offered Him — He would not be made king by force (John 6:15), and would not come down from the cross to prove Himself (Matthew 27:40–42). He stayed inside His own assignment, and that is precisely how we were saved.
10.code: “I cannot go with these” is a complete sentence.

quiz.q: Who armed David with his armour?
What did David say about the armour?
What did David do after saying no to the armour?

11.title: Remember Your Testimony

scripture.text: The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.

11.truth: Past deliverance is a promise, not a memory.
11.hook: You keep a record of everything. Where do you keep the record of what God has done?

points.title: Testimony is the answer to intimidation.
points.body: “The LORD that delivered me out of the paw of the lion, and out of the paw of the bear, he will deliver me out of the hand of this Philistine.”

points.title: Past deliverance is a promise, not a memory.
points.body: He used a finished act of God as evidence for an unfinished one.

points.title: Keep receipts.
points.body: If you cannot recall what God has done, you will over-fear what is in front of you.

11.illustration: “The LORD that delivered me…” Confidence grows when you remember what God has already done.
11.challenge: Open your lion-and-bear page from Day 4. Read it out loud to one person today.
questions: What is your testimony? Have you told anyone? (Revelation 12:11)

mirrors.ot: Samuel set up a stone and called it Ebenezer — “Hitherto hath the LORD helped us” (1 Samuel 7:12).
mirrors.nt: “They overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony” (Revelation 12:11).

11.christ: The greatest testimony ever given is an empty tomb — “He is not here: for he is risen” (Matthew 28:6). David testified to a lion and a bear. We testify to a resurrection. If death could not hold Him, your giant cannot hold you.
11.code: Past deliverance is a promise, not a memory.

quiz.q: Which two animals did David's testimony name?
What is past deliverance, according to the day?
What did Samuel name the stone he set up?

12.title: I Come in His Name

scripture.text: Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel, whom thou hast defied.

12.truth: The Name settles the outcome before the fight.
12.hook: Raises the sling — “This was his weapon.” Raises the empty hand — “This is where his confidence was.”

points.title: Goliath came with hardware; David came with a Name.
points.body: “Thou comest to me with a sword, and with a spear, and with a shield: but I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts.”

points.title: He developed a sling and depended on a Name.
points.body: Both. Never one without the other — that is the whole balance of this series.

points.title: The Name settles the outcome before the fight.
points.body: “This day will the LORD deliver thee into mine hand.”

12.illustration: David's greatest confidence wasn't his sling; it was God's Name.
12.challenge: Before today's hardest moment, say out loud: “I come in the name of the Lord.”
questions: What are you trusting in that is not the Name of the Lord? (Philippians 2:9–11)

mirrors.ot: “Some trust in chariots, and some in horses: but we will remember the name of the LORD our God” (Psalm 20:7) — written by this same David, years later. He never changed weapons.
mirrors.nt: “In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk” (Acts 3:6). No silver, no gold — the Name.

12.christ: David borrowed that Name by faith. We know it by revelation: “God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name” (Philippians 2:9–11). Jesus. That is the Name your SuperPower runs on.
12.code: The Name settles the outcome before the fight.

quiz.q: What did Goliath come with?
options: Hardware: a sword, a spear and a shield

quiz.q: What did David come with?
Which Name does the day's Christ point name as above every name?

14.title: Is There Not a Cause?

scripture.text: Is there not a cause?

14.truth: A cause is what keeps you standing when people misread you.
14.hook: A child raises a hand to volunteer; a sibling yanks it straight back down. Freeze frame. Presenter: "The first person who tries to stop you usually shares your surname."

points.title: Eliab attacked his character, not his argument
points.body: "I know thy pride, and the naughtiness of thine heart." When people cannot answer you, they redefine you.

points.title: David did not defend himself; he pointed at the mission.
points.body: "Is there not a cause?" Conviction keeps the main thing the main thing.

points.title: A cause is what keeps you standing when people misread you.
points.body: Without one, criticism stops you. With one, it barely slows you down.

14.illustration: Great people live for something bigger than themselves.
14.challenge: When someone discourages you today, do not defend yourself. Ask "is there not a cause?" — and get back to work.
14.declaration: My life will solve a problem bigger than myself.
questions: What "great work" must you not come down from? (Nehemiah 6:3)

mirrors.ot: Nehemiah to his mockers: "I am doing a great work, so that I cannot come down" (Nehemiah 6:3).
mirrors.nt: "A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house" (Matthew 13:57).

14.christ: "Neither did his brethren believe in him" (John 7:5) — and yet He said, "I must work the works of him that sent me" (John 9:4). Jesus had the greatest cause ever carried, and He carried it through the doubt of His own family. His brother James later became a pillar of the church. Keep going; doubters can become disciples.

quiz.q: What did David point to instead of defending himself?
options: The mission: "Is there not a cause?"

quiz.q: According to the lesson, what does a cause do when people misread you?
What does Eliab's attack show, according to the lesson?
options: He attacked David's character, not his argument
He was David's brother by blood only

15.title: See the Problem
15.truth: Whoever sees it is usually the one sent to solve it.
15.hook: The same shouting clip plays four times, louder each time, until it is uncomfortable. Cut to total silence. Presenter, calmly: "Forty days of that. Everybody heard him." Beat. "One boy actually looked at him."

points.title: Hearing and seeing are not the same thing.
points.body: The army heard a threat. David saw a situation with a solution in it.

points.title: Familiarity makes people stop looking.
points.body: Forty days had turned a solvable problem into normal weather. Conviction refuses to call a problem "just how things are."

points.title: Whoever sees it is usually the one sent to solve it.
points.body: If you can see it clearly and it bothers you deeply, look closer — that may be your assignment.

15.illustration: Everybody heard Goliath. David saw a problem that could be solved.
15.challenge: Walk through your day today looking, not just listening. Write down one problem you saw that nobody seems to be fixing.
questions: What did you see today that others walked past? (Matthew 9:36)

mirrors.ot: Nehemiah heard about broken walls and "sat down and wept, and mourned certain days" — then went and rebuilt them (Nehemiah 1:3–4). Everyone knew the walls were broken. One man saw it.
mirrors.nt: "But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them... Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest" (Matthew 9:36–38). Seeing came first; sending came after.

15.christ: Jesus saw what everybody else walked past — Zacchaeus in a tree (Luke 19:5), a widow's two mites (Mark 12:42), one woman in a crowded street (Mark 5:30–32). Ask Him for His eyes and He will show you your problem.
15.code: One boy actually looked at him.

quiz.q: What does the lesson say the army did?
options: Saw a situation with a solution in it
Prayed for the Lord of the harvest

quiz.q: What did forty days do to the problem, according to the lesson?
If a problem bothers you deeply and you can see it clearly, what does the lesson suggest?
options: Look closer, it may be your assignment

16.title: Feel the Reproach

scripture.text: Who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?

16.truth: What breaks your heart is often the map to your assignment.
16.hook: Presenter sits, leans in, quiet. "I want to ask you a question almost nobody asks children." Long beat. "What makes you angry?" Beat. "Not annoyed. Angry."

points.title: He was offended by the right thing.
points.body: "Who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?" Not "he might hurt me" — "he is disgracing God's people."

points.title: Holy anger is a compass.
points.body: What breaks your heart is often the map to your assignment. Pay attention to what you cannot walk past.

points.title: Feeling is not enough — David felt it and then moved.
points.body: Conviction that never becomes action is just an opinion.

16.illustration: David cared that Israel was being disgraced. What bothers you may point toward your assignment.
16.challenge: Finish this sentence honestly: "It bothers me that ______." Bring that sentence to God tonight and ask Him what it means.
questions: What breaks your heart? Have you ever asked God why? (Romans 15:3)

mirrors.ot: Moses "spied an Egyptian smiting an Hebrew" and something in him could not accept it (Exodus 2:11–12). The instinct was right even when his method was not — and God spent forty years shaping it into deliverance.
mirrors.nt: Paul in Athens: "his spirit was stirred in him, when he saw the city wholly given to idolatry" (Acts 17:16) — and that stirring became one of the greatest sermons ever preached.

16.christ: Jesus wept over a city (Luke 19:41) and drove out the money changers because "my house shall be called the house of prayer" (Matthew 21:13). He felt the reproach on His Father's name — and then He carried the reproach Himself: "the reproaches of them that reproached thee are fallen upon me" (Romans 15:3).

quiz.q: Why was David offended, according to the lesson?
options: The king had not paid him

quiz.q: What does the lesson call holy anger?
What does the lesson say about conviction that never becomes action?
options: It is the same as prayer

17.title: Ask Better Questions

scripture.text: What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine?

17.hook: Two children look at the same photograph. First: "That's scary." Second: "How do we fix it?" Presenter to camera: "Same picture. Same day. Two completely different futures."

points.title: Your questions set your direction.
points.body: The soldiers asked about the threat. David asked "What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine?" Same field, different future.

points.title: He asked more than once and asked around.
points.body: "And he turned from him toward another, and spake after the same manner" (17:30). He gathered information instead of absorbing atmosphere.

points.title: Outcome questions beat obstacle questions.
points.body: Faith is not the absence of the problem; it is a bigger interest in the promise.

17.illustration: "What shall be done…?" David asked different questions from everyone else.
17.challenge: Take the thing worrying you most. Write one fear question and one faith question about it. Answer only the faith one.
questions: What would change today if God opened your eyes to what He is doing? (2 Kings 6:17)

mirrors.ot: Elisha's servant panicked at an encircling army; Elisha prayed "LORD, open his eyes" — and the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire (2 Kings 6:15–17). Same hill, better question.
mirrors.nt: Mary asked "How shall this be?" — not to doubt but to understand — and then said "be it unto me according to thy word" (Luke 1:34, 38).

17.christ: Jesus taught almost entirely in questions — "Whom say ye that I am?" (Matthew 16:15); "What wilt thou that I shall do unto thee?" (Mark 10:51). He is not afraid of your questions. He is the answer to them.

quiz.q: Which question did David ask?
options: What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine?

quiz.q: How did David gather information, according to the lesson?
options: He asked more than once and asked around
He asked only once and stopped

quiz.q: What does the lesson say faith is?
options: A bigger interest in the promise

18.title: Discover Your Problem

scripture.text: Who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?

18.truth: Every assignment is a problem with somebody's name on it.
18.hook: Presenter points straight down the lens and says nothing for four full seconds. "Today is not about David." Beat. "Today is about you. And there is only one question." Beat. "What problem has your name on it?"

points.title: Every assignment is a problem with somebody's name on it.
points.body: David's name was on a giant. Nehemiah's was on a wall. Esther's was on a decree. Yours is on something.

points.title: Start where you already are.
points.body: Your school, your family, your street, your nation — in that order. Do not wait to be somewhere impressive.

points.title: "For such a time as this."
points.body: Esther 4:14 — you were put in this exact place, in this exact year, on purpose. 2026/2027 is not a random session for you.

18.illustration: What problem in your school, family, community or nation do you want to solve?
18.challenge: Write down one problem you want your life to help solve. School, family, community or nation. Write it clearly enough that somebody else could read it.
questions: Why do you think God put you exactly where you are, in exactly this year? (Esther 4:14)

mirrors.ot: Esther — "who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?" (Esther 4:14). Her position was her assignment.
mirrors.nt: "Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit" (John 15:16).

18.christ: Jesus knew exactly what problem He came to solve and said it out loud in a synagogue — "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor... to set at liberty them that are bruised" (Luke 4:18). He read His assignment publicly and then went and did it.
18.code: What problem has your name on it?

quiz.q: What does the lesson say Esther's position was?
According to the lesson, what did Jesus say His assignment was in the synagogue?
options: To preach the gospel to the poor

quiz.q: Where does the lesson say you should start?

19.title: Find Your Cause

scripture.text: David, after he had served his own generation by the will of God, fell on sleep

19.truth: Your capacity is the tool; your cause is the reason.
19.hook: Two cards held up: WHAT I DO and WHY I DO IT. Presenter tears the first one in half. "You can win at this one" — holds up the torn half — "and still waste your entire life."

points.title: Career answers "what." Cause answers "why."
points.body: A career can be taken from you. A cause goes with you into every room you ever enter.

points.title: A cause outlives the person carrying it.
points.body: "David, after he had served his own generation by the will of God, fell on sleep" (Acts 13:36). That is the whole obituary — he served his generation.

points.title: Your capacity is the tool; your cause is the reason.
points.body: This is why we develop anything at all. Not so you can be amazing — so you can be useful.

19.illustration: Your career is what you do. Your cause is why you do it.
19.challenge: Take Friday's problem and turn it into a sentence: "I want to spend my life helping to ______." Say it out loud to one adult who loves you.
questions: If someone wrote one sentence about your life, what do you want it to say? (Acts 13:36)

mirrors.ot: Joseph's whole hard story had one sentence under it: "God did send me before you to preserve life" (Genesis 45:5). The cause explained the years.
mirrors.nt: Paul: "But none of these things move me... so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus" (Acts 20:24).

19.christ: "For this cause came I unto this hour" (John 12:27). Jesus had the greatest cause in history — to seek and save the lost — and He finished it: "It is finished" (John 19:30). Every cause a child of God carries is a branch of His.
19.code: Career answers what. Cause answers why.

quiz.q: Which question does a career answer, according to the lesson?
What goes with you into every room you enter?
According to Acts 13:36, how did David serve?

21.title: Go Towards the Giant

scripture.text: David hasted, and ran toward the army to meet the Philistine.

21.hook: Slow motion. A crowd running hard in one direction; one child running straight through them the other way. Freeze on the child. Presenter: "Everybody in this shot is behaving normally." Beat. "Except one person."

points.title: The direction of your feet reveals the state of your heart.
points.body: Israel "fled from him, and were sore afraid" (17:24). David "hasted, and ran toward."

points.title: Courage closes the distance.
points.body: Fear negotiates from far away. Courage walks up to the thing.

points.title: Moving toward it makes it smaller.
points.body: Every problem you avoid grows in the dark. The giant was never bigger than on the day nobody approached him.

21.illustration: David "hasted, and ran toward the army." Courage moves toward problems.
21.challenge: Do the one thing today you have been avoiding — the apology, the question in class, the difficult conversation. Move toward it.
21.declaration: I will not bury what God has put inside me.
questions: What are you running away from that God is asking you to run toward? (Joshua 1:9)

mirrors.ot: Caleb at eighty-five: "Now therefore give me this mountain" (Joshua 14:12). Ten spies fled giants; Caleb asked for their address.
mirrors.nt: Peter: "Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water" (Matthew 14:28–29). Eleven stayed seated. One walked.

21.christ: "He stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem" (Luke 9:51). Jesus ran toward the cross knowing exactly what waited there — "who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross" (Hebrews 12:2). Our courage is borrowed from His.

quiz.q: What does the lesson say the direction of your feet reveals?
What did Israel do when they saw Goliath, according to 17:24?
options: Fled from him, and were sore afraid

quiz.q: What does the lesson say happens to a problem you avoid?

22.title: Start With What You Have

scripture.text: He chose him five smooth stones out of the brook.

22.truth: He used what was already in his hand.
22.hook: Five stones dropped into a leather bag, one at a time, in silence. Presenter looks up. "That is it. That is the entire armoury." Beat. "And it was too much — he only needed one."

points.title: He used what was already in his hand.
points.body: Not what he wished he had. Not what the king offered. What he had developed.

points.title: He chose deliberately.
points.body: "He chose him five smooth stones out of the brook." Not the first five he touched. Courage is prepared, not reckless.

points.title: He took more than he needed.
points.body: One stone did it — he carried five. Preparation always carries margin.

22.illustration: A sling and five stones looked insignificant until David used them.
22.challenge: Choose your five stones for the 2026/2027 session: five habits you will carry into the new term. Write them down and name them out loud.
questions: What is already in your hand that you have been calling too small? (Exodus 4:2)

mirrors.ot: God asked Moses, "What is that in thine hand?" — an ordinary shepherd's rod became the rod of God (Exodus 4:2).
mirrors.nt: A boy brought five loaves and two fish and Jesus fed five thousand (John 6:9–11). Small, surrendered, multiplied.

22.christ: "Take unto you the whole armour of God" (Ephesians 6:11–17) — truth, righteousness, peace, faith, salvation, the Word. Every piece of the real equipment is found in Christ. He is the armour that always fits.

quiz.q: What did David use, according to the lesson?
options: What was already in his hand

quiz.q: How many stones did David carry?
How many stones did he actually need?

23.title: Stop Comparing
23.truth: Comparison always makes you the loser.
23.hook: Bronze armour on the left of frame, a leather sling on the right. Presenter stands between them. "One of these looked serious." Beat. "The other one won."

points.title: Comparison always makes you the loser.
points.body: There is always someone taller, faster, richer. The moment you measure yourself against them, you stop developing yourself.

points.title: Your difference may be your advantage.
points.body: Goliath's whole battle plan assumed an armoured man walking slowly toward him. He had no answer for a fast boy with a range weapon.

points.title: God does not duplicate.
points.body: He never made two of you, so there is nothing to compare.

23.illustration: Saul had armour. David had a sling. Your difference may be your advantage.
23.challenge: Notice the moment today you compare yourself to someone. Stop, and thank God for one thing He put in you instead.
questions: Who have you been comparing yourself to, and what has it cost you? (1 Corinthians 1:27)

mirrors.ot: Gideon's three hundred, chosen precisely because they were few — "lest Israel vaunt themselves against me, saying, Mine own hand hath saved me" (Judges 7:2).
mirrors.nt: "God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and... the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty" (1 Corinthians 1:27).

23.christ: When Peter compared himself to John, Jesus answered, "What is that to thee? follow thou me" (John 21:22). Comparison is a distraction from your own following. Christ has a path with your name on it, not a copy of somebody else's.
23.code: Your difference may be your advantage.

quiz.q: What did Goliath's battle plan assume, according to the lesson?
options: A fast boy with a range weapon
An armoured man walking slowly toward him

quiz.q: What does the lesson say comparison always does?
What does 'God does not duplicate' mean in the lesson?
options: He never made two of you

24.title: Courage Before Confidence

scripture.text: Let no man's heart fail because of him; thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine.

24.truth: Courage is not the absence of fear.
24.hook: Presenter holds out a visibly shaking hand to camera. "People think courage means this stops." Hand keeps shaking. "It doesn't." Beat. "You just move anyway."

points.title: Courage is not the absence of fear.
points.body: God kept telling brave people "fear not" — which means they were afraid. Fear is not disqualification.

points.title: Confidence often arrives after the first step, not before it.
points.body: David steadied the room — "Let no man's heart fail" — and then volunteered. He led with action, not with feelings.

points.title: Obedience does not wait to feel ready.
points.body: If you wait until you feel ready, you will still be waiting when the session ends.

24.illustration: Sometimes you have to move while you are still afraid.
24.challenge: Do one thing today while you are still nervous about it. Do not wait for the feeling to change.
questions: What are you waiting to feel ready for? What if ready never comes? (2 Timothy 1:7)

mirrors.ot: "Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed" (Joshua 1:9) — God said it to Joshua three times in one chapter. Repeated commands answer real fear.
mirrors.nt: "God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind" (2 Timothy 1:7).

24.christ: In Gethsemane Jesus was "sore amazed, and very heavy" and prayed "let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt" (Matthew 26:37–39). He felt everything — and went anyway. That is courage, and He gives it away: "In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world" (John 16:33).

quiz.q: What does the lesson say courage is not?
What did David say to steady the room?
What does the lesson say happens if you wait until you feel ready?
options: You will still be waiting when the session ends
You will feel ready at once

25.title: Take the Shot

scripture.text: David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it.

25.hook: A sling winding up, faster and faster. Freeze at full stretch. Presenter, over the frozen frame: "Every stone he ever threw in that field was for this one second." Beat. "And all of it is worth nothing until he lets go."

points.title: Preparation has an expiry point.
points.body: "David put his hand in his bag, and took thence a stone, and slang it." All the practice in the world does nothing until the hand releases.

points.title: One well-developed shot was enough.
points.body: He did not need all five. Develop deeply, then act decisively.

points.title: Unused capacity becomes buried talent.
points.body: The servant in Jesus' parable did not lose the talent — he just never used it, and that was the failure.

25.challenge: Take one action today on the cause you wrote on Day 16. One phone call, one conversation, one first step. Today.
questions: What has God given you that you have buried instead of used? (Matthew 25:25–27)

mirrors.ot: The four lepers at the gate of Samaria: "Why sit we here until we die?" (2 Kings 7:3–9). They moved, and the whole city ate.
mirrors.nt: "Thou wicked and slothful servant... thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers" (Matthew 25:26–27). The sin was not losing it. The sin was burying it.

25.christ: "I must work the works of him that sent me, while it is day: the night cometh, when no man can work" (John 9:4). Jesus lived with holy urgency and finished everything He was sent to do. He is both our example and our power to act.

quiz.q: What does the lesson say preparation has?
How many stones did David need, according to the lesson?
What was the failure of the servant in Jesus' parable?

26.title: Run Toward Responsibility

scripture.text: thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine.

26.truth: Responsibility is the gym of capacity.
26.hook: Two doors, marked EASY and HARD. Presenter opens EASY — an empty room. Closes it. Opens HARD — a gym full of weights. "Both doors are open to you today." Beat. "Only one of them builds you."

points.title: Responsibility is the gym of capacity.
points.body: Nobody grows carrying nothing. Every hard assignment you accept enlarges what you can hold.

points.title: David volunteered
points.body: "thy servant will go and fight with this Philistine." He was not drafted. He raised his hand.

points.title: The avoided assignment does not disappear; it waits.
points.body: And it is still there in the new session, only bigger.

26.illustration: Capacity grows when you stop avoiding difficult assignments.
26.challenge: Volunteer for one thing this week that nobody wants to do. At home, at school, or at church.
questions: What responsibility have you been avoiding, and what is it costing you? (Luke 12:48)

mirrors.ot: Isaiah heard "Whom shall I send?" and answered "Here am I; send me" (Isaiah 6:8) — a volunteer, not a conscript.
mirrors.nt: "Unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required" (Luke 12:48). Capacity and responsibility rise together, always.

26.christ: "Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God" (Hebrews 10:7). Jesus is the ultimate volunteer — He took the one responsibility nobody else could carry, and carried it to the end.

quiz.q: Who volunteered, according to the lesson?
What does the lesson say an avoided assignment does?
options: Waits, and is still there, only bigger

quiz.q: What does the lesson compare responsibility to?

28.title: Kill Your Giant

scripture.text: So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone.

28.truth: Development is measured by outcome, not effort.
28.hook: The CAVE → CONQUEST board, four panels lit, the fifth dark. Presenter walks the length of it. "Four weeks. Twenty-three days. All of it developing something nobody could see." Lights the fifth panel. "Today we find out what it was for."

points.title: Development is measured by outcome, not effort.
points.body: "So David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone." Four weeks of preparation, one sentence of result.

points.title: He finished it.
points.body: "There was no sword in the hand of David" (17:50) — so he used Goliath's own sword. God ends the enemy's story with the enemy's weapon.

points.title: The giant did not create David's capacity. It revealed it.
points.body: Everything that fell in that valley was developed in a field where nobody was watching. This is the big idea of the whole month — say it out loud today.

28.challenge: Finish one thing today that you started and abandoned. Do not leave it at ninety percent.
28.declaration:
I will build in The Cave.
I will stand in The Covenant.
I will live for The Cause.
I will act with Courage.
I will produce Conquest.
questions: What is one thing you want to be able to say you finished this year? (2 Timothy 4:7)

mirrors.ot: Joseph's years in a prison were revealed as preparation the moment he stood before Pharaoh (Genesis 41:14–41). Nothing wasted, all of it useful.
mirrors.nt: "I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith" (2 Timothy 4:7). Paul measured his life by what he finished.

28.christ: At Calvary the enemy's own weapon — death — became the instrument of his defeat: "that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death" (Hebrews 2:14). Jesus said "It is finished" (John 19:30). We do not fight for victory. We fight from it.

quiz.q: What does the lesson say development is measured by?
What sword did David use, according to the lesson?
What did the giant do to David's capacity, according to the lesson?

29.title: Make Others Brave

scripture.text: The men of Israel and of Judah arose, and shouted, and pursued the Philistines.

29.truth: One person's courage releases a generation.
29.hook: One child stands up. Beat. A second stands. Beat. Then the entire room is on its feet. Presenter, over the top: "Nobody told them to do that." Beat. "They just needed to see it done once."

points.title: One person's courage releases a generation.
points.body: "The men of Israel and of Judah arose, and shouted, and pursued the Philistines." They had been in that valley forty days. They only needed someone to go first.

points.title: They pursued what they used to run from.
points.body: Same army, same enemy, brand new courage. Capacity is contagious.

points.title: Your victory raises the ceiling for everybody watching.
points.body: Somebody in your class, your street, your family is waiting to see it done once.

29.illustration: After David defeated Goliath, the entire army arose. Real capacity doesn't only change you; it changes what other people believe is possible. The echo, 2 Samuel 21:22: “These four were born to the giant in Gath, and fell by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.” David killed one giant; his servants killed four more. Real capacity does not just win. It reproduces.
29.challenge: Name one person you will help stand this term. Tell them today that you believe they can.
questions: Who is watching you? What are they learning is possible? (1 Samuel 17:52)

mirrors.ot: Deborah arose "a mother in Israel" and Barak and ten thousand followed (Judges 4:8–10; 5:7).
mirrors.nt: "When they saw the boldness of Peter and John... they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus" (Acts 4:13). The credential was His company — and the whole city noticed.

29.christ: Jesus is the greater David: He went out alone on our behalf, defeated the enemy we could never face, and shares the victory with everyone standing behind Him — "Thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ" (1 Corinthians 15:57). And He said, "He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also" (John 14:12). He does not just win; He multiplies winners.

quiz.q: Who arose and pursued the Philistines?
options: The men of Israel and of Judah

quiz.q: What does the lesson say capacity is?
What did David's servants do, according to the echo in 2 Samuel 21:22?

30.title: Become God's Answer

scripture.text: David, after he had served his own generation by the will of God, fell on sleep

30.truth: God is not looking for the amazing. He is looking for the available.
30.hook: The full board, all five panels blazing. Presenter walks into frame and stops. "Thirty days ago you were a person with potential." Beat. Looks straight down the lens. "Today you are a person with a plan."

points.title: Capacity travels outward in stages.
points.body: Reproach removed → enemy defeated → army awakened → nation served. It started with one boy and one gift, developed in private.

points.title: God is not looking for the amazing. He is looking for the available.
points.body: "David, after he had served his own generation by the will of God, fell on sleep" (Acts 13:36). One sentence, one whole life: he served his generation.

points.title: You are entering 2026/2027 as an answer.
points.body: Not as a student hoping to survive the session — as somebody God has spent September preparing to use.

30.illustration: David's capacity removed reproach → defeated an enemy → awakened an army → served a nation.
30.challenge: Stand where you are. Say your five stones out loud. Say your cause sentence out loud. Then name the one person you will help stand this term.
questions: You are a city set on a hill. What will your light do in this new session? (Matthew 5:14–16)

mirrors.ot: "God did send me before you to preserve life" (Genesis 45:5). Joseph's whole story had one purpose under it, and he only saw it at the end.
mirrors.nt: "Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid... Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven" (Matthew 5:14–16).

30.christ: Every SuperPower this month has one source. "I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me" (Philippians 4:13). David developed a sling; God delivered the giant. You develop your gift; God delivers the outcome. And the reason any of it matters is Him: "for of him, and through him, and to him, are all things" (Romans 11:36).

quiz.q: What order does the lesson give for capacity travelling outward?
options: Reproach removed, enemy defeated, army awakened, nation served

quiz.q: What is the closing question of the month?
options: What problem will my capacity solve?

quiz.q: What does the lesson say God is looking for?

1.title: The Cave · Competence
1.recap:
The cave is not punishment.

- Chant: Stanza 1, three times, with actions.
- Both lines together: Teach the open and close lines until the children can finish them.
- Recap round: Five children, one sentence each on Days 1–5.
- Declaration together: “I will develop privately until I can deliver publicly.”
- Testimony slot: Who did a good thing nobody found out about? Now they may tell.
- The gift roll-call: Go round the room — every child names the one gift they are practising for fifteen minutes a day. Write them all up somewhere visible. This is the spine of the whole month.
- Expect this question: “How long do I have to stay hidden?” Answer honestly: until God moves you, and He is never late. The cave is not punishment.
- Parents: Name one hidden faithfulness you have noticed in your child this week — out loud, in front of them.
- Look ahead: “Next week we find out where David's confidence actually came from. It was not his size.”
1.reading: For who hath despised the day of small things? (Zechariah 4:10)
questions: What small thing are you tempted to despise? (Zechariah 4:10)
1.declaration: I will develop privately until I can deliver publicly.

2.title: The Covenant · Confidence
2.recap:
You find it by using what is already in your hand, not by waiting for a feeling.

- Chant: Stanzas 1 + 2.
- Recap round: Six children, one sentence each on Days 6–11.
- Declaration together: “I know who I am, whose I am, and what God has put inside me.”
- The “I am” wall: Every child reads out one of the three sentences they wrote on Day 6. Put them on a wall and leave them there all month.
- Testimony slot: Who took off borrowed armour this week? Who refused to change themselves to fit in?
- Expect this question: “What if I don't know what God put inside me yet?” Answer: you find it by using what is already in your hand, not by waiting for a feeling.
- Parents: Affirm what is uniquely theirs about your child — not what makes them like a sibling or a cousin.
- Look ahead: “Next week we find out what David was actually angry about. It wasn't the giant's size.”
2.reading: For thou hast possessed my reins: thou hast covered me in my mother's womb... I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. (Psalm 139:13–16)
questions: Which of God's descriptions of you is hardest for you to believe? (Psalm 139:13–16)
2.declaration: I know who I am, whose I am, and what God has put inside me.

3.title: Discussion 3 — The Cause (Conviction)
3.recap:
My life will solve a problem bigger than myself.

- Chant: Stanzas 1 + 2 + 3.
- Recap round: Six children, one sentence each on Days 12–17.
- Declaration together: "My life will solve a problem bigger than myself."
- The cause roll-call — the centrepiece of the month: Every child who is willing stands and says their sentence: "I want to spend my life helping to ______." Write every single one down. Some children are telling you their future in that sentence — give this the time it deserves and do not rush it into the next item.
- Testimony slot: Who saw a problem this week that others walked past?
- Expect this question: "What if my cause is small?": Answer: David's cause was one giant in one valley. It changed a nation. Start where your name is.
- Parents: Ask your child their sentence this week and take it seriously. Do not correct it. Write it down.
- Look ahead: "You can have capacity and never use it. Next week is about fear."
3.reading: But none of these things move me... so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus (Acts 20:24)
questions: What would it take for you to finish your course with joy? (Acts 20:24)
3.declaration: My life will solve a problem bigger than myself.

4.title: Discussion 4 — The Courage (Use What You Have)
4.recap:
I will not bury what God has put inside me.

- Chant: Stanzas 1 + 2 + 3 + 4.
- Recap round: Six children, one sentence each on Days 18–23.
- Declaration together: "I will not bury what God has put inside me."
- The five stones: Every child who is willing says their five habits for the new session out loud. Write them up beside the "I am" wall and the cause sentences. By now that wall is the story of your whole month — photograph it.
- Testimony slot: Who moved while still afraid this week? Who took a first step on their cause?
- Expect this question: "What if I take the shot and I miss?": Answer honestly: you will miss things. David carried five stones for a reason. Missing is part of developing; burying is not.
- Parents: Give your child one genuinely difficult responsibility this week and let them carry it fully.
- Look ahead: "Three days left. Monday, the giant finally falls — and we find out what capacity is really for."
4.reading: Thou wicked and slothful servant... thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers (Matthew 25:14–29)
questions: Which servant are you being with what God has given you? (Matthew 25:14–29)
4.declaration: I will not bury what God has put inside me.

stewardship-code.title: The Stewardship Code
stewardship-code.subtitle: Secrets to Managing Money
stewardship-code.tagline: Christ my Master, money my servant.

themeScripture.text: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much.

declaration: God owns everything.
I am only a steward.
I will give an account.
Money is a tool, never my master.
Christ my Master — money my servant.

weeks.title: God Owns It; I Manage It
weeks.question: Whose money, time and talents am I managing?

weeks.title: Manage Little Before More
weeks.question: Can God trust me with what is already in my hands?

weeks.title: Christ My Master, Money My Servant
weeks.question: Do I control money, or has money begun to control me?

weeks.title: Build It, Grow It, Send It Ahead
weeks.question: What am I doing to increase what God placed in my hands?

1.title: CRACK THE STEWARDSHIP CODE

scripture.text: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

1.truth:
Money must never become the master of our hearts. God gives us money as a tool to manage,
deploy and use for His purposes.

points.title: Everyone Serves a Master
points.body:
Jesus did not say that having money is wrong. He warned that serving money is wrong.

A master is anything that controls your choices, commands your loyalty and determines your
priorities.

Money becomes a master when:

- You disobey God to obtain it.
- You lie to keep it.
- You measure your worth by it.
- You cannot release it when God directs you to give.
- You place financial gain above righteousness.

The first question in stewardship is not, “How much money do I have?”

It is, “Who rules my heart?”

points.title: Money Was Created to Serve
points.body:
Money can be used to:

- Buy food.
- Pay school fees.
- Support families.
- Build businesses.
- Spread the gospel.
- Educate children.
- Solve community problems.
- Create opportunities.

Money is powerful, but it must remain in its proper position.

It must remain in your hand and never sit on the throne of your heart.

points.title: Stewardship Is Management Under God
points.body:
A steward is not the final owner. A steward manages what belongs to someone else.

God owns everything, but He entrusts different portions of His resources to different
people.

He expects us to manage those resources:

- Faithfully
- Wisely
- Honestly
- Productively
- Generously
- Eternally

supporting.text: The earth is the LORD’S, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.
And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.

1.illustration:
Imagine a powerful car without a driver.

The car may have speed, strength and value, but without someone controlling it, it can cause
destruction.

Money is like that car.

It can take you forward when properly directed, but it can destroy lives when it is allowed
to control the driver.

You must remain in the driver’s seat under the direction of Jesus Christ.
1.challenge:
Write down your honest answers to these three questions:

- What do I currently believe money can do for me?
- What financial pressure most easily controls my emotions?
- How can I begin making money serve God’s purpose?
1.prayer:
Father, teach me the secrets of faithful stewardship. Deliver my heart from greed, fear,
comparison and the love of money. Let Jesus Christ remain my Master, and teach me to make
money a useful servant. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
1.declaration:
Jesus Christ is my Master.
Money is my servant.
I will learn and live the Stewardship Code.
1.transition: Before we can learn how to manage money, we must first settle the question of ownership.

2.title: THE OWNER

scripture.text: The earth is the LORD’S, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.

2.truth:
Everything belongs to God. Stewardship begins when we stop acting like absolute owners and
begin living as responsible managers.

points.title: God Owns the World
points.body:
The earth did not create itself, and we did not bring ourselves into existence.

God created:

- The land
- The oceans
- The minerals
- The plants
- The animals
- Human intelligence
- Human strength
- Every opportunity for productivity

Therefore, God is not merely one participant in the economy. He is the ultimate Owner of
everything within it.

points.title: God Owns What Is in Your Hands
points.body:
Your phone may have your name on it. Your parents may have purchased it. But the materials,
intelligence, health and opportunity that made the purchase possible came from God.

God owns:

- Your time
- Your abilities
- Your education
- Your possessions
- Your opportunities
- Your future
- Your influence

You are responsible for how these resources are used.

points.title: Ownership Changes Behaviour
points.body:
When you understand that something belongs to God, you treat it differently.

You will be less likely to:

- Waste it.
- Destroy it.
- Use it for sin.
- Neglect it.
- Compare it carelessly.
- Take it for granted.

The awareness of God’s ownership creates responsibility.

supporting.text: The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts.

Thine, O LORD, is the greatness, and the power, and the glory, and the victory, and the majesty: for all that is in the heaven and in the earth is thine; thine is the kingdom, O LORD, and thou art exalted as head above all.

2.illustration:
Suppose a friend lends you an expensive laptop for a week.

Because the laptop belongs to someone else, you would probably:

- Carry it carefully.
- Keep food and water away from it.
- Avoid dangerous downloads.
- Return it on time.
- Report any problem immediately.

You would treat it carefully because you know you are accountable to the owner.

Your life and resources should be treated with even greater care because they belong to God.
2.challenge:
Create a list titled:

#### “What God Owns but Has Placed in My Hands”

Include at least seven things, such as time, money, devices, skills and opportunities.
2.prayer:
Father, open my eyes to see that everything belongs to You. Deliver me from wastefulness and
entitlement. Help me manage every resource as something entrusted to me by You. In Jesus’
name. Amen.
2.declaration:
God owns everything.
Everything in my hands belongs to Him.
2.transition: If God is the Owner, what does that make us?

3.title: THE STEWARD

scripture.text: And he said also unto his disciples, There was a certain rich man, which had a steward; and the same was accused unto him that he had wasted his goods.

3.truth: A steward manages another person’s resources according to the owner’s instructions.

points.title: A Steward Is a Manager
points.body:
The steward in Luke 16 was responsible for the rich man’s property.

He did not own the resources, but he had:

- Access
- Authority
- Opportunity
- Responsibility

Being a steward means God allows us to handle resources that still belong to Him.

points.title: Access Is Not Ownership
points.body:
Having access to something does not mean you can use it carelessly.

You may have access to:

- Your parents’ money
- A family car
- School equipment
- Church property
- Internet access
- A leadership position
- Another person’s trust

Access creates responsibility. It does not remove accountability.

points.title: A Steward Must Be Faithful
points.body:
The most important quality of a steward is not popularity, intelligence or wealth.

It is faithfulness.

Faithfulness means:

- Doing what is right consistently.
- Protecting what has been entrusted.
- Following instructions.
- Producing the expected result.
- Remaining honest when nobody is watching.

supporting.text: Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.
As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.

3.illustration:
A school prefect has authority, but the prefect does not own the school.

The prefect cannot invent personal rules merely to impress friends. The authority was given
to serve the school’s purpose.

In the same way, God gives us resources and influence to serve His purposes, not merely to
please ourselves.
3.challenge:
Choose one resource from yesterday’s inventory and answer:

- Why has God placed this in my hands?
- Who can it help?
- How can I manage it better?
3.prayer:
Lord, make me a faithful steward. Help me use every privilege, possession and opportunity
according to Your purpose. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
3.declaration:
I am not the ultimate owner.
I am God’s faithful steward.
3.transition:
A steward must know not only who owns the resources but also where those resources came
from.

4.title: THE SOURCE

scripture.text: But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto thy fathers, as it is this day.

4.truth:
God is the Source. Money, jobs, businesses and opportunities are channels through which His
provision may come.

points.title: God Gives the Power to Produce
points.body:
Money does not normally fall from heaven.

It may come through:

- Work
- Business
- Creativity
- Skill
- Investment
- Gifts
- Opportunities

But behind every legitimate channel is the God who gives:

- Life
- Health
- Intelligence
- Strength
- Favour
- Ideas
- Relationships
- Opportunity

Never worship the channel and forget the Source.

points.title: The Source Is Greater Than the Resource
points.body:
A resource can finish.

A job may end. A customer may leave. A gift may be spent. An opportunity may change.

But God remains.

When your trust is in God, you can remain peaceful even when one channel of provision
changes.

points.title: Remembering God Produces Humility
points.body:
Success can make people say:

- “I did it all by myself.”
- “Nobody helped me.”
- “I do not need anyone.”
- “My intelligence gave me everything.”

The Bible tells us to remember the Lord because remembrance protects us from pride.

supporting.text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.
But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly after this sort? for all things come of thee, and of thine own have we given thee.

4.illustration:
A child receives ₦5,000 from a parent and uses ₦500 to buy the parent a birthday gift.

The gift is meaningful, but the money originally came from the parent.

In the same way, everything we offer to God first came from Him.
4.challenge:
Write down three channels through which God currently provides for you.

Beside each one, write:

“God is my Source; this is only a channel.”
4.prayer:
Father, help me remember You in every season of success. Keep me humble and grateful. Let my
confidence remain in You and not merely in money or people. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
4.declaration:
God is my Source.
Money is only a resource.
4.transition: If God gives us resources, then those resources must carry an assignment.

5.title: THE ASSIGNMENT

scripture.text: And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.

5.truth:
Every resource God gives carries an assignment. We must discover what it was given to
accomplish.

points.title: God Gives Resources for a Reason
points.body:
The master did not give the servants money merely to admire or display.

He expected them to use it productively.

God gives resources so they can:

- Meet needs
- Build capacity
- Create value
- Bless people
- Support families
- Advance His Kingdom
- Produce a responsible increase

points.title: Every Resource Has Potential
points.body:
A phone can become:

- A distraction
- A classroom
- A camera
- A business tool
- A Bible
- A design studio
- A communication platform

The object may be the same, but the assignment determines how it is used.

points.title: Ask Purpose Before Pleasure
points.body:
Before using a resource, ask:

- Why did God allow me to have this?
- What good can it accomplish?
- What problem can it solve?
- Who can it help?
- How can it honour God?

Pleasure is not automatically sinful, but purpose must lead pleasure.

supporting.text: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.
And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.

5.illustration:
Two teenagers receive identical smartphones.

One uses the phone mainly for endless scrolling and entertainment.

The other learns video editing, designs flyers, studies courses and helps a church media
team.

The difference is not the device. The difference is purpose.
5.challenge: Select one resource you own and write three productive assignments it can fulfil.
5.prayer:
Lord, show me the purpose of everything You have placed in my hands. Deliver me from using
valuable resources only for temporary pleasure. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
5.declaration:
Everything God gives me has an assignment.
I will use it for His purpose.
5.transition: Because every resource has an assignment, every steward must eventually give a report.

6.title: THE ACCOUNT

scripture.text: And he called him, and said unto him, How is it that I hear this of thee? give an account of thy stewardship; for thou mayest be no longer steward.

6.truth: Every steward will eventually explain what was done with what was received.

points.title: God Keeps Records
points.body:
The steward’s management was reviewed.

In the same way, God sees:

- How we use our time
- How we handle money
- How we treat people
- How we develop our abilities
- How we respond to opportunities
- How we use our influence

Nothing entrusted to us is outside His concern.

points.title: Accountability Improves Responsibility
points.body:
Knowing that an assignment will be graded changes how a serious student approaches it.

In the same way, knowing that we will give an account should help us:

- Plan better
- Waste less
- Obey faster
- Work diligently
- Remain honest
- Live intentionally

points.title: Accountability Is Personal
points.body:
Each person must answer for his or her own stewardship.

You cannot blame:

- Your friends
- Your parents
- Your school
- Your siblings
- Social media
- Your background

These things may influence you, but you must still make responsible choices.

supporting.text: So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God.
For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.

6.illustration:
A student who knows there will be an examination does not wait until the examiner enters the
room before beginning to learn.

The coming examination influences today’s preparation.

Eternal accountability should influence today’s stewardship.
6.challenge:
Review how you used the following during the past seven days:

- Time
- Money
- Internet access
- Talents
- Opportunities

Write one improvement beside each area.
6.prayer:
Father, help me live with accountability. Give me wisdom to manage today in a way that will
please You when I give my report. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
6.declaration: I will manage today because I will report tomorrow.
6.transition: Tomorrow, we will gather the lessons of the Ownership Code into a personal covenant.

7.title: THE OWNERSHIP COVENANT

scripture.text: But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly after this sort? for all things come of thee, and of thine own have we given thee.

7.truth: Everything belongs to God, and everything in our hands must be managed as a sacred trust.

points.title: God Is the Owner
points.body:
This week, we learned that God owns:

- The world
- Silver and gold
- Our abilities
- Our opportunities
- Our time
- Our lives

God is not asking to become part-owner. He already owns everything.

points.title: I Am the Steward
points.body:
A steward receives:

- Resources
- Responsibility
- Instructions
- Opportunity

A steward must respond with faithfulness.

The question is not merely, “What do I have?”

The better question is, “How am I managing what belongs to God?”

points.title: My Life Is an Assignment
points.body:
Your life is not an accident.

Your abilities, environment, relationships and opportunities can become tools through which
God’s purpose is fulfilled.

Stewardship means turning what God has given you into service, value and impact.

supporting.text: Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.
The earth is the LORD’S, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.

7.illustration:
A trusted courier may carry a package worth millions of naira.

The package may be in the courier’s hands, but it does not belong to the courier.

The courier’s success is measured by whether the package reaches the right destination in
the right condition.

Your success as a steward is measured by whether God’s resources fulfil God’s assignment
through your life.
7.challenge:
Your life is not an accident.

Your abilities, environment, relationships and opportunities can become tools through which
God’s purpose is fulfilled.

Stewardship means turning what God has given you into service, value and impact.
7.prayer:
Father, I acknowledge You as the Owner of my life and everything connected to me. Make me a
faithful steward. Let every resource in my hands fulfil Your purpose. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

8.title: FAITHFUL IN LITTLE

scripture.text: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.

8.truth:
Little resources are not meaningless. They are tests that reveal whether we are ready for
greater responsibility.

points.title: Little Reveals Character
points.body:
Many people say:

- “I will save when I earn more.”
- “I will give when I become rich.”
- “I will become responsible when I have a business.”
- “I will stop wasting money when I receive more.”

Jesus teaches that behaviour in little predicts behaviour in much.

points.title: More Does Not Repair Bad Habits
points.body:
If a person wastes ₦1,000, the same person may waste ₦100,000.

A larger income does not automatically create:

- Discipline
- Wisdom
- Integrity
- Contentment
- Generosity

These qualities must be developed before increase arrives.

points.title: Little Is Training
points.body:
Small amounts teach you how to:

- Record
- Budget
- Save
- Give
- Delay gratification
- Make choices
- Resist pressure

Do not despise the training ground.

supporting.text: For who hath despised the day of small things? for they shall rejoice, and shall see the plummet in the hand of Zerubbabel with those seven; they are the eyes of the LORD, which run to and fro through the whole earth.
His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.

8.illustration:
A leaking bucket does not first need more water.

It needs the leak repaired.

Pouring more water into a leaking bucket only creates a larger waste.

Before asking God for more, identify and repair the leaks in your present stewardship.
8.challenge:
Identify three small resources you currently manage.

For each one, write one habit that would demonstrate faithfulness.
8.prayer:
Father, help me become faithful in little. Teach me not to despise small beginnings or delay
discipline until increase comes. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
8.declaration:
My little is not useless.
My little is my test.
8.transition: To manage faithfully, you must first know what you have and where it is going.

9.title: KNOW WHAT YOU HAVE

scripture.text: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.

9.truth: You cannot manage accurately what you refuse to measure.

points.title: Good Stewards Pay Attention
points.body:
In Bible times, flocks and herds represented wealth.

The owner had to know:

- How many animals were present
- Which ones were healthy
- Which ones were missing
- Which ones were growing
- Which ones required attention

Modern stewardship also requires awareness.

points.title: Records Reveal Reality
points.body:
You may feel that you do not spend much, but written records may reveal otherwise.

Keeping records helps you see:

- Repeated purchases
- Wasteful habits
- Emotional spending
- Forgotten debts
- Missed savings
- Giving patterns

Facts help you make better decisions.

points.title: Measure More Than Money
points.body:
Teenagers should also track:

- Time
- Internet use
- Screen time
- Study hours
- Skill development
- Commitments
- Personal goals

Every important resource deserves attention.

supporting.text: Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established.
So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.

9.illustration:
Your phone can show how much data or battery each application consumes.

Without checking the report, you may blame the wrong app.

In the same way, a money record reveals which habits are consuming your resources.
9.challenge:
Track every amount you receive and spend for seven days.

Use these headings:

- Date
- Amount Received
- Amount Spent
- Purpose
- Need or Want
- Balance
9.prayer:
