Lord, give me discipline to measure what You place in my hands. Help me face my habits
honestly and make wise corrections. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
9.declaration:
I measure what I manage.
I improve what I measure.
9.transition: Once you know what you have, the next step is to give every amount an assignment.

10.title: PLAN BEFORE YOU SPEND

scripture.text: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?

10.truth: A budget is a plan that gives money an assignment before emotions spend it.

points.title: Planning Is Biblical
points.body:
Jesus used the picture of a builder who first counted the cost.

Planning is not a lack of faith.

Wise planning helps you:

- Understand what is required
- Set priorities
- Prepare for future needs
- Avoid unnecessary debt
- Complete what you begin

points.title: A Budget Protects Priorities
points.body:
Without a budget, the loudest desire may take all the money.

A simple teenage budget can include:

- Give
- Save
- Spend
- Invest
- Learn
- Help

A budget ensures that important things are not ignored.

points.title: A Budget Gives You Freedom
points.body:
Some people think a budget is a punishment.

A good budget actually gives you permission to spend within agreed limits.

It protects you from:

- Regret
- Impulse
- Peer pressure
- Confusion
- Constant shortage

supporting.text: The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.
There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man spendeth it up.

10.illustration:
A football team does not enter a match with every player running wherever he feels like
running.

The team uses a formation.

A budget is a financial formation. It puts every part of your money in the right position.
10.challenge:
Create a budget for your next allowance, gift or income.

Use percentages or actual amounts under these headings:

- Giving
- Saving
- Spending
- Investing
- Learning
10.prayer:
Father, give me wisdom to plan before I spend. Help me control impulses and direct my
resources towards worthwhile purposes. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
10.declaration: I will direct my money before it disappears.
10.transition: Faithfulness is also revealed by how we treat what belongs to another person.

11.title: FAITHFUL WITH ANOTHER PERSON’S

scripture.text: And if ye have not been faithful in that which is another man’s, who shall give you that which is your own?

11.truth:
How you treat what belongs to others reveals whether you are ready for greater personal
responsibility.

points.title: Borrowed Things Are a Test
points.body:
When you borrow something, you should:

- Ask permission
- Use it carefully
- Return it promptly
- Return it in good condition
- Report any damage honestly

Carelessness with borrowed property reveals poor stewardship.

points.title: Shared Resources Also Belong to Someone
points.body:
School, family and church property may feel as though they belong to nobody.

But they belong to a community.

Examples include:

- Chairs
- Books
- Toilets
- Computers
- Sports equipment
- Musical instruments
- Electricity
- Water

Responsible people protect shared resources.

points.title: Trust Opens Doors
points.body:
People entrust greater opportunities to those who have demonstrated responsibility.

If you are faithful with:

- Someone else’s time
- Someone else’s money
- Someone else’s idea
- Someone else’s equipment
- Someone else’s confidence

You become a person who can be trusted with more.

supporting.text: Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.
And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.

11.illustration:
Two students borrow cameras.

The first student returns the camera clean, fully charged and safely packed.

The second returns it late with a missing cover and a scratched lens.

Which student will be trusted with the more expensive camera next time?
11.challenge:
Do one of the following today:

- Return something you borrowed.
- Repair something you damaged.
- Replace something you lost.
- Clean a shared space.
- Ask forgiveness for careless handling.
11.prayer:
Father, make me trustworthy with what belongs to others. Help me protect every resource
placed in my care. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
11.declaration: I honour God by caring for what belongs to another.
11.transition: Faithfulness is not only about careful handling. It is also about integrity.

12.title: CHARACTER BEFORE CASH

scripture.text: If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?

12.truth: Money tests character. Integrity must be stronger than the desire for quick profit.

points.title: Money Reveals the Heart
points.body:
Money can reveal:

- Greed
- Fear
- Dishonesty
- Pride
- Generosity
- Contentment
- Self-control

Money does not always create character problems. It often exposes what was already present.

points.title: Integrity Is More Valuable Than Profit
points.body:
Never exchange your character for:

- Extra change
- Examination malpractice
- Internet fraud
- Stolen property
- False advertising
- Secret commissions
- Dishonest business

Money gained through corruption carries a cost greater than its value.

points.title: True Riches Require Trust
points.body:
Jesus spoke of “true riches.”

God values things money cannot purchase:

- Wisdom
- Integrity
- Spiritual understanding
- Trust
- Good character
- Kingdom responsibility

Financial faithfulness can prepare us to carry these greater treasures.

supporting.text: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.
Better is the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than he that is perverse in his ways, though he be rich.

12.illustration:
A cashier mistakenly gives a teenager ₦5,000 more than the correct change.

Nobody else notices.

Returning the money shows that the teenager’s integrity is worth more than temporary gain.
12.challenge:
Examine your recent financial actions.

Correct any dishonest act involving:

- Change
- Borrowing
- Selling
- School payments
- Online transactions
- Shared money
12.prayer:
Lord, build my character before increasing my cash. Give me courage to remain honest even
when dishonesty appears profitable. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
12.declaration: I will never exchange integrity for income.
12.transition: Faithfulness is not one good action. It is a consistent pattern.

13.title: THE FAITHFULNESS TEST

scripture.text: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.

13.truth: God examines how we handle little before entrusting greater responsibility.

points.title: Faithfulness Is Consistent
points.body:
Faithfulness means doing what is right:

- Repeatedly
- Quietly
- Correctly
- Promptly
- Honestly

It is not one impressive action followed by weeks of carelessness.

points.title: Faithfulness Requires Systems
points.body:
Good intentions are not always enough.

Simple systems help you become faithful:

- Keep records
- Use a budget
- Save automatically
- Return borrowed items
- Set reminders
- Review spending
- Ask for accountability

Systems make responsible behaviour easier to repeat.

points.title: Faithfulness Prepares You for Increase
points.body:
The goal is not merely to receive more money.

Faithfulness prepares you for:

- Greater trust
- Greater influence
- Greater opportunities
- Greater responsibility
- Greater impact

God’s promotion is larger than financial increase.

supporting.text: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.
A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent.

13.illustration:
Brushing your teeth for one hour once a month cannot replace brushing for a few minutes
every day.

Many results come through consistency, not occasional intensity.
13.challenge:
Create your four-part Faithfulness System:

- What will I record?
- What will I save?
- What will I stop wasting?
- Who will hold me accountable?
13.prayer:
Father, make me faithful in little. Give me discipline, honesty and consistency. Prepare my
character for every increase You desire to place in my hands. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

14.title: TWO MASTERS

scripture.text: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

14.truth: Jesus Christ must remain the only Master of our hearts. Money must remain a servant.

points.title: A Master Demands Loyalty
points.body:
A master has the right to command.

If money is your master, it will command you to:

- Chase it at any cost
- Compromise your values
- Compare yourself with others
- Fear constantly
- Ignore people
- Disobey God

Jesus deserves complete loyalty.

points.title: Mammon Is More Than Currency
points.body:
Mammon represents the power, confidence and identity people attach to money.

Money becomes mammon when you believe:

- Money is your ultimate security.
- Money determines your value.
- Money can solve every problem.
- Life has no meaning without wealth.
- God’s instructions can be ignored for profit.

points.title: You Must Choose
points.body:
Jesus did not present serving God and mammon as a comfortable partnership.

One must remain above the other.

The Christian order is:

- Christ is Master.
- I am His steward.
- Money is my servant.

supporting.text: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

14.illustration:
Two people cannot safely hold and turn the steering wheel of the same moving car in opposite
directions.

There must be one recognised driver.

There must also be one recognised Master in your life.
14.challenge:
Complete this sentence honestly:

“Money most often tries to control me through __________.”

Then write one biblical response to that pressure.
14.prayer:
Jesus Christ, remain the only Master of my heart. Deliver me from every form of loyalty to
mammon. Let money remain beneath Your authority. Amen.
14.declaration: Jesus Christ alone is my Master.
14.transition: Money becomes dangerous when it takes the place that belongs to God.

15.title: GOLD IS NOT MY GOD

scripture.text: For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.

15.truth: Money itself is not evil, but loving money can corrupt faith, character and relationships.

points.title: The Bible Condemns the Love of Money
points.body:
The verse does not say that money is the root of all evil.

It warns against the love of money.

The love of money appears when people:

- Crave wealth above righteousness
- Measure everyone by possessions
- Use people to gain profit
- Refuse contentment
- Abandon faith for financial advantage

points.title: Money Makes a Poor God
points.body:
Money cannot:

- Forgive sin
- Give eternal life
- Heal every disease
- Guarantee peace
- Create genuine love
- Replace family
- Satisfy the soul

Money can solve financial problems, but it cannot carry the weight of worship.

points.title: Enjoy Resources Without Worshipping Them
points.body:
God may bless people with resources.

The correct response is to:

- Give thanks
- Remain humble
- Share generously
- Use wisely
- Refuse pride
- Maintain devotion to Christ

supporting.text: Trust not in oppression, and become not vain in robbery: if riches increase, set not your heart upon them.
Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.

15.illustration:
Fire is valuable when it remains in a fireplace or cooker.

It can provide warmth and prepare food.

But when fire takes over the house, it destroys what it was meant to serve.

Money must remain in its proper place.
15.challenge:
List three things money cannot give you.

Then list three ways money can be used responsibly.
15.prayer:
Father, cleanse my heart from the love of money. Help me enjoy Your provision without
worshipping possessions. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
15.declaration:
Gold is not my god.
Jesus Christ is my Lord.
15.transition: Money can also control us through the possessions we use to define ourselves.

16.title: POSSESSIONS MUST NOT POSSESS ME

scripture.text: And he was sad at that saying, and went away grieved: for he had great possessions.

16.truth: Possessions become dangerous when they control our identity, confidence and obedience.

points.title: The Rich Young Ruler Owned Much
points.body:
The young man had many possessions.

His wealth was not the only problem.

The deeper issue was that he could not release what stood between him and obedience to
Jesus.

What he owned had gained control over his heart.

points.title: Identity Must Come From Christ
points.body:
Teenagers may be tempted to build identity around:

- Phones
- Shoes
- Clothes
- Cars
- Schools
- Neighbourhoods
- Social media appearance

These things can be enjoyed, but they must never determine personal worth.

points.title: Attachment Is Revealed by Release
points.body:
You may not know how attached you are to something until you are asked to:

- Share it
- Give it
- Delay it
- Lose it
- Live without it
- Choose obedience over it

A steward can release possessions because identity and security are found in God.

supporting.text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.

16.illustration:
A teenager feels confident only when wearing a particular brand of shoe.

Without it, the teenager feels inferior.

The shoe is no longer merely being worn. It has started controlling the teenager’s sense of
worth.
16.challenge:
Choose one possession you value highly.

Write:

- Why do I value it?
- How would I feel without it?
- Does it affect how I see myself?
- Could I share or release it if God required it?
16.prayer:
Father, let my identity remain rooted in Christ. Deliver me from allowing possessions,
brands or appearances to control my confidence. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
16.declaration:
I possess things.
Things do not possess me.
16.transition: One of the strongest forces behind unnecessary spending is pressure.

17.title: NEEDS, WANTS AND PRESSURE

scripture.text: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.

17.truth: Contentment gives us the strength to separate genuine needs from wants created by pressure.

points.title: Needs and Wants Are Different
points.body:
A need is something necessary for health, safety, responsibility or basic functioning.

A want is something desirable but not essential.

A want is not automatically wrong, but calling every want a need creates poor financial
decisions.

points.title: Pressure Can Distort Desire
points.body:
Pressure may come from:

- Friends
- Advertisements
- Influencers
- Trends
- Fear of missing out
- Comparison
- The desire to impress

Pressure can turn a useful desire into an emotional emergency.

points.title: Contentment Is Learned
points.body:
Paul said, “I have learned.”

Contentment does not mean:

- Refusing to grow
- Rejecting improvement
- Avoiding ambition
- Remaining careless

Contentment means you can be grateful and peaceful while working responsibly for
improvement.

supporting.text: But godliness with contentment is great gain.
Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.

17.illustration:
A teenager has a phone that performs every necessary function.

After seeing friends with newer phones, the teenager begins to feel that the present phone
is useless.

The device did not suddenly stop working. Comparison changed the teenager’s feelings.
17.challenge:
For every purchase you consider today, classify it as:

- Need
- Useful want
- Pressure-driven want

Delay any pressure-driven purchase for at least seven days.
17.prayer:
Lord, teach me contentment. Help me resist comparison and emotional spending. Give me wisdom
to recognise needs, wants and pressure. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
17.declaration:
I will not spend to impress people.
My identity is secure in Christ.
17.transition: Money stops controlling us when we deliberately give it a godly assignment.

18.title: GIVE MONEY AN ASSIGNMENT

scripture.text: And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.

18.truth:
Money becomes a servant when it is deliberately directed towards meaningful and eternal
purposes.

points.title: Money Is a Tool
points.body:
A tool cannot decide what it will build.

The person holding the tool gives it direction.

Money can be directed to:

- Feed
- Educate
- Build
- Support
- Create
- Invest
- Give
- Solve

Money should receive instructions from a wise steward.

points.title: Earning Should Lead to Impact
points.body:
The goal of work is not only personal consumption.

Biblical earning can provide resources to:

- Meet personal responsibilities
- Help family
- Give to others
- Support Kingdom work
- Build solutions
- Create jobs
- Develop skills

Income should become impact.

points.title: Give Before Money Controls You
points.body:
Generosity breaks the illusion that money must be held at all costs.

Giving reminds the heart:

- God is my Source.
- Money is not my security.
- People matter.
- I can release resources.
- I am a steward, not an owner.

supporting.text: Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth.
He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.

18.illustration:
A teenager uses part of a holiday income to purchase books for a younger student who cannot
afford them.

The money is no longer merely currency. It has become an instrument of education and hope.
18.challenge:
Give part of your money, time or skill to meet one genuine need today.

Do it quietly and intentionally.
18.prayer:
Father, teach me to give money a godly assignment. Let my resources solve problems, build
people and advance Your purposes. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
18.declaration: My money must serve God’s mission.
18.transition:
Tomorrow, we will identify and break the chains through which mammon tries to control the
heart.

19.title: BREAK MAMMON’S CHAINS

scripture.text: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

19.truth:
Financial freedom begins when Jesus Christ is Master and money is deliberately kept in the
position of a servant.

points.title: Mammon Chains Through Disobedience
points.body:
Money is becoming a master when you are willing to:

- Lie for it
- Cheat for it
- Steal for it
- Abandon worship for it
- Betray trust for it
- Hurt people for it

No amount of money is worth losing obedience to Christ.

points.title: Mammon Chains Through Identity
points.body:
Money is becoming a master when your confidence rises and falls according to:

- Your possessions
- Your family’s status
- Your clothes
- Your phone
- Your ability to impress people

Your identity must be anchored in Christ.

points.title: Mammon Chains Through Fear
points.body:
Money may control people by making them constantly afraid of:

- Not having enough
- Losing what they possess
- Being seen as poor
- Missing an opportunity
- Helping others
- Trusting God

Wise planning is good. Constant financial fear is another form of bondage.

supporting.text: Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed?
He that trusteth in his riches shall fall: but the righteous shall flourish as a branch.

19.illustration:
A prisoner may be connected to a chain made of gold.

The chain may look expensive, but it is still a chain.

Wealth, possessions and status can appear attractive while still keeping a heart in bondage.
19.challenge:
Practise one act of financial freedom:

- Give something.
- Delay a purchase.
- Reject peer pressure.
- Admit a dishonest action.
- Help someone.
- Save instead of showing off.
- Thank God for what you already possess.
19.prayer:
Jesus Christ, break every chain of mammon in my heart. Deliver me from greed, fear,
comparison and material pride. Remain my Master, and teach me to direct money as Your
steward. Amen.

20.title: OCCUPY UNTIL HE COMES

scripture.text: And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.

20.truth:
Jesus expects His servants to remain spiritually faithful and productively engaged until He
returns.

points.title: Occupy Means Engage Productively
points.body:
The servants were not told to sit beside the money and wait.

They were instructed to put it to work.

Christian faith should produce:

- Diligence
- Creativity
- Responsibility
- Service
- Enterprise
- Productivity

Waiting for Christ is not an excuse for laziness.

points.title: Work Can Honour God
points.body:
Work is not merely a way to receive money.

Work can:

- Serve people
- Develop character
- Create solutions
- Build communities
- Express excellence
- Honour God

Productive work is part of stewardship.

points.title: Prayer and Action Belong Together
points.body:
Prayer is essential, but prayer should lead us into obedient action.

We should:

- Pray for wisdom.
- Plan carefully.
- Learn diligently.
- Work honestly.
- Review results.
- Improve continuously.

supporting.text: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.
And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.

20.illustration:
A farmer cannot pray over an empty field and expect a harvest without planting seed.

Prayer invites God’s wisdom and help. Work puts that wisdom into action.
20.challenge: Spend at least thirty minutes developing a productive skill today.
20.prayer:
Lord, make me productive while I wait for Your return. Deliver me from laziness and teach me
to work heartily as unto You. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
20.declaration: I will pray, plan, work and produce.
20.transition: The greatest enemy of multiplication is burying what God has given.

21.title: DO NOT BURY IT

scripture.text: And another came, saying, Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin.

21.truth:
God does not give us gifts merely to preserve them. He expects us to develop and deploy
them.

points.title: Preservation Is Not Always Faithfulness
points.body:
The servant returned exactly what he received.

Nothing was stolen, but nothing was multiplied.

He protected the resource from loss but also prevented it from producing value.

Playing safe can become disobedience when God has instructed us to act.

points.title: Fear Buries Gifts
points.body:
People may hide their abilities because they fear:

- Failure
- Criticism
- Embarrassment
- Comparison
- Rejection
- Imperfection

Fear may keep a gift safe, but it also keeps the gift unproductive.

points.title: Gifts Grow Through Use
points.body:
A gift develops when you:

- Practise
- Learn
- Receive correction
- Attempt difficult tasks
- Serve others
- Repeat consistently

Unused ability remains undeveloped potential.

supporting.text: Wherefore I put thee in remembrance that thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands.
A man’s gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.

21.illustration:
A musical instrument may be beautifully designed and extremely expensive.

But if it remains permanently inside its case, it produces no music.

Your gifts must come out of hiding.
21.challenge:
Choose one gift or skill you have neglected.

Practise it for at least thirty minutes and share the result with a trusted person.
21.prayer:
Father, deliver me from fear. Help me stir up, develop and deploy every gift You have placed
within me. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
21.declaration: I will not bury what God expects me to build.
21.transition: A gift becomes increasingly valuable when it is intentionally developed.

22.title: DEVELOP YOUR GIFT

scripture.text: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.

22.truth: Natural ability becomes valuable through diligence, training and consistent improvement.

points.title: Potential Is Only a Beginning
points.body:
Potential means you could become good at something.

It does not mean you have already developed mastery.

Potential must be followed by:

- Practice
- Study
- Discipline
- Feedback
- Experience
- Improvement

points.title: Diligence Creates Distinction
points.body:
Diligence means giving careful, consistent effort.

Diligent teenagers:

- Arrive prepared
- Practise basics
- Ask questions
- Correct mistakes
- Meet deadlines
- Continue learning

Excellence is often the accumulated result of small acts of diligence.

points.title: Skill Creates Opportunity
points.body:
People are often willing to pay for:

- Useful knowledge
- Reliable service
- Creative ability
- Technical skill
- Clear communication
- Problem-solving capacity

Developing a gift can create opportunities for service, influence and income.

supporting.text: Then this Daniel was preferred above the presidents and princes, because an excellent spirit was in him; and the king thought to set him over the whole realm.
Meditate upon these things; give thyself wholly to them; that thy profiting may appear to all.

22.illustration:
A naturally talented footballer may initially perform better than others.

But if the talented player refuses training while another player practises daily, the
disciplined player may eventually become far better.

Talent gives a beginning. Diligence produces growth.
22.challenge:
Create a seven-day development plan for one skill.

Include:

- What you will practise
- How long you will practise
- What resource you will study
- Who will give feedback
- What result you hope to produce
22.prayer:
Lord, give me diligence. Help me develop every ability You have placed within me and use it
with excellence. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
22.declaration: I will practise until my gift produces value.
22.transition: Developed gifts become especially valuable when they solve real problems.

23.title: SOLVE A PROBLEM

scripture.text: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Forasmuch as God hath shewed thee all this, there is none so discreet and wise as thou art.

23.truth: Value is created when wisdom, skills and resources are used to solve genuine problems.

points.title: Joseph Saw More Than a Crisis
points.body:
Egypt faced a future famine.

Joseph did not merely identify the problem. He presented:

- A plan
- A system
- A storage strategy
- A leadership structure
- A long-term solution

His ability to solve the problem created opportunity and influence.

points.title: Problems Can Become Opportunities to Serve
points.body:
Around you, people may struggle with:

- Difficult school subjects
- Technology
- Transportation
- Organisation
- Cleaning
- Design
- Communication
- Access to useful information

A steward asks, “What can I do to help?”

points.title: Income Often Follows Value
points.body:
People normally exchange money for something they value.

That value may be:

- A product
- A service
- Convenience
- Knowledge
- Entertainment
- Safety
- Time saved
- A problem solved

Do not only ask, “How can I make money?”

Also ask, “What valuable problem can I solve?”

supporting.text: Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.
When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth: and when the wicked perish, there is shouting.

23.illustration:
A student notices that younger children struggle with mathematics.

The student organises simple revision lessons, prepares worksheets and helps the children
improve.

Knowledge has become a solution. The solution may also become a source of responsible
income.
23.challenge:
Write down three problems around you.

For each problem, answer:

- Who experiences it?
- What causes it?
- What skill could help?
- What small solution can I test?
23.prayer:
Father, give me eyes to see needs and wisdom to create solutions. Let my gifts become
valuable to my generation. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
23.declaration: I create value by solving problems.
23.transition: A wise steward does not consume every result. Part must be preserved and multiplied.

24.title: MULTIPLY, DON’T CONSUME EVERYTHING

scripture.text: Then came the first, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds.

24.truth:
A steward preserves and multiplies part of today’s resources instead of consuming everything
immediately.

points.title: Consumption Uses Resources Today
points.body:
Consumption is necessary.

We must spend on:

- Food
- Clothing
- Transport
- Education
- Responsibilities
- Appropriate enjoyment

The problem begins when everything is consumed and nothing is preserved.

points.title: Saving Preserves Resources
points.body:
Saving means setting aside part of today’s income for future use.

Saving can prepare you for:

- Emergencies
- Education
- Business tools
- Opportunities
- Future purchases
- Investments
- Giving

Saving gives your future self resources.

points.title: Investment Seeks Responsible Growth
points.body:
Investment places resources into something that may produce future value.

Teenagers can begin by investing in:

- Books
- Courses
- Skills
- Tools
- Small projects
- Productive equipment
- Carefully supervised financial instruments

Investment should involve learning, patience and wise guidance.

supporting.text: Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished: but he that gathereth by labour shall increase.
Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:

24.illustration:
Two teenagers receive the same holiday income.

The first spends everything on entertainment and fashion.

The second enjoys some, saves some and buys tools to begin a simple service.

They started equally, but their stewardship created different futures.
24.challenge:
For your next income, create a multiplication allocation:

- Give
- Save
- Spend
- Invest
- Learn

Set aside the saving and investment portions before spending.
24.prayer:
Father, deliver me from consuming everything. Give me wisdom to save, invest and multiply
responsibly. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
24.declaration: I am a creator and multiplier, not merely a consumer.
24.transition: The highest purpose of multiplication is not personal accumulation. It is eternal impact.

25.title: INVEST FOR ETERNITY

scripture.text: And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.

25.truth: Temporary resources should be used in ways that produce lasting and eternal impact.

points.title: Money Is Temporary
points.body:
Money can:

- Be spent
- Be lost
- Lose value
- Be stolen
- Become outdated
- Remain behind when life ends

Because money is temporary, it should be directed towards things of lasting value.

points.title: People Have Eternal Value
points.body:
Using resources to build people can produce long-term impact.

You can invest in people through:

- Education
- Mentoring
- Encouragement
- Food
- Training
- Gospel outreach
- Medical care
- Community development

The greatest return is not always measured in money.

points.title: Kingdom Investment Sends Treasure Ahead
points.body:
Jesus taught us to lay up treasure in heaven.

Kingdom investment includes:

- Supporting the gospel
- Helping the vulnerable
- Serving people
- Giving generously
- Using gifts for God’s glory
- Building lives
- Obeying God with resources

These investments produce rewards that outlive earthly possessions.

supporting.text: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:
While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.

25.illustration:
An expensive outfit may look impressive for a season, but it will eventually wear out or
become unfashionable.

The same amount invested in a child’s education, spiritual growth or useful skill may
influence an entire lifetime.
25.challenge:
Create your Personal Multiplication Plan:

- One gift I will develop
- One problem I will solve
- One amount I will save
- One investment I will study
- One person I will help
- One Kingdom project I will support
25.prayer:
Father, teach me to use temporary resources for eternal purposes. Help me develop, multiply
and deploy everything You place in my hands for Your glory. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

26.title: THE FAITHFUL STEWARD

scripture.text: His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.

26.truth:
The final goal of stewardship is to hear Jesus Christ say, “Well done, good and faithful
servant.”

points.title: The Faithful Steward Recognises Ownership
points.body:
The faithful steward understands:

- God owns everything.
- God is the Source.
- Every resource carries an assignment.
- Access is not absolute ownership.
- Every steward will give an account.

This understanding produces humility and responsibility.

points.title: The Faithful Steward Manages and Multiplies
points.body:
The faithful steward:

- Records resources
- Plans before spending
- Remains honest
- Protects what belongs to others
- Develops gifts
- Solves problems
- Saves consistently
- Invests wisely
- Produces value

Faithfulness is active, not passive.

points.title: The Faithful Steward Serves Christ
points.body:
The greatest test is not how much money you possess.

It is whether Jesus Christ remains your Master.

A faithful steward can possess wealth without being possessed by wealth.

The order remains:

- Christ is my Master.
- I am His steward.
- Money is my servant.
- People are more valuable than possessions.
- Eternity guides my decisions.

supporting.text: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.
And he said unto him, Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.

26.illustration:
A servant may carry the king’s treasure.

The treasure may pass through the servant’s hands, but the servant must never mistake
himself for the king.

Wealth may pass through your hands, but it must never sit on the throne of your heart.
26.challenge:
Write and sign the Stewardship Covenant below.

Add:

- Your full name
- The date
- One financial habit you will begin
- One wasteful habit you will stop
- One skill you will develop
- One person or cause you will support

## FINAL STEWARDSHIP COVENANT

> Everything I am and everything I possess belongs to God.
> I am not the ultimate owner. I am His steward.
> I will manage faithfully, spend wisely, save consistently, give generously and multiply responsibly.
> I will not serve money or build my identity around possessions.
> I will use my gifts, time, knowledge, opportunities and resources to solve problems, build people and glorify God.
> I will remain faithful in little while preparing responsibly for much.
> I will use temporary resources to produce eternal impact.
> Jesus Christ will remain my Master, and money will remain my servant.
> Name: ______________________________
> Signature: ___________________________
> Date: _______________________________

0.title: Series Opening: Whose Money Is It?
0.recap:
Yesterday we cracked open the month: **everyone serves a master**, and money is either a
useful servant or a cruel god (Ep 1). Tomorrow we begin **THE OWNERSHIP CODE** — *God owns
it; I manage it.* This week's question: *Whose money, time, talents and opportunities am I
managing?*
0.reading:
Read **Luke 16:1–13** — the parable of the shrewd manager, our anchor text for the whole
month.

*As you read, look for:* the word **steward**. Notice the manager never owned anything. He
was accused of wasting what belonged to someone else — and he still had to give an account.
questions: Jesus said you cannot serve God and mammon. Where in ordinary life does money quietly
The manager was fired for *wasting*, not stealing. What's the difference — and does that
If God owns everything in your room right now, what would you handle differently
0.prayer:
Father, before we learn how to manage money, settle the question of ownership in our hearts.
You are the Owner; we are Your stewards. Let Jesus Christ be our only Master and let money
stay our servant. In Jesus' name. Amen.
0.declaration:
Christ my Master!
Money my servant!

1.title: Week 1 Recap: THE OWNERSHIP CODE
1.recap:
**THE OWNERSHIP CODE — God owns it; I manage it.** We met **the Owner**: the earth, the
silver and the gold are all His (Ep 2). We learned who we are — **the steward**, a manager
of someone else's goods (Ep 3). We traced every ability and opportunity back to **the
Source** (Ep 4). We discovered that every resource carries an **assignment** (Ep 5), and
that one day every steward gives **an account** (Ep 6). Yesterday you signed the **Ownership
Covenant** and built your Personal Resource Inventory.
1.reading:
Read **Psalm 24:1–2**, then **Luke 16:1–2** together.

*As you read, look for:* the two halves of the code. Psalm 24 says who owns it. Luke 16 says
what the owner eventually asks for — *"Give an account of thy stewardship."*
questions: What was the hardest item on your Resource Inventory to hand back and call God's?
Episode 4 said God is the *Source*, not just the supplier. How does remembering the
"Give an account of thy stewardship." If that review happened this week, what would you
1.prayer:
Father, You are the Owner of our lives and everything connected to us. Deliver us from
entitlement and waste. Show us the assignment behind every resource You have placed in our
hands, and keep us ready to give an account. In Jesus' name. Amen.
1.declaration:
God owns everything.
I am only a steward.
My life is an assignment.
I will be ready to give an account.

2.title: Week 2 Recap: THE FAITHFULNESS CODE
2.recap:
**THE FAITHFULNESS CODE — manage little before asking for more.** We learned that little is
not small; it is **training** (Ep 8). We started to **know what we have**, because records
reveal reality (Ep 9). We learned to **plan before we spend**, and that a budget is freedom,
not a cage (Ep 10). We were tested with **what belongs to someone else** (Ep 11), and we
chose **character before cash** (Ep 12). Yesterday's **Faithfulness Test** asked the honest
question: *can God trust me with what is already in my hands?*
2.reading:
Read **Luke 16:10–12** — three verses, the whole code.

*As you read, look for:* how many times "little" and "much" appear together. Faithfulness in
the least is never separate from faithfulness in much — it *is* the qualification for it.
questions: Where did you find a leak this week once you actually started keeping records?
Verse 12 is about *another person's* things. How do we treat what we borrow — and what
More money never repairs bad habits. Which single habit are you carrying into next week?
2.prayer:
Father, make us faithful in the little that is already in our hands. Give us honest records,
wise plans and clean character. We would rather be trustworthy than wealthy — and we trust
You for the increase in Your time. In Jesus' name. Amen.
2.declaration:
I will be faithful before increase.
Money will remain a tool, never my master.

3.title: Week 3 Recap: THE MASTERY CODE
3.recap:
**THE MASTERY CODE — Christ my Master, money my servant.** We faced the choice between **two
masters** (Ep 14). We said out loud that **gold is not my god**, because the love of money —
not money itself — is the root of evil (Ep 15). We refused to let **possessions possess us**
(Ep 16). We learned to tell the difference between **needs, wants and pressure** (Ep 17), and
to **give money an assignment** before it invents one for us (Ep 18). Yesterday we named the
three chains of mammon — disobedience, identity and fear — and broke them.
3.reading:
Read **Luke 16:9–13**, then **1 Timothy 6:6–10**.

*As you read, look for:* what Jesus tells us to *do* with money in verse 9 — use it to bless
people and serve eternal purposes — right before He says in verse 13 that we cannot serve it.
questions: Which chain has the strongest grip in your life right now — disobedience, identity or
Contentment is *learned*, not automatic. What did you practise this week that helped?
Name one purchase you almost made because of pressure. What did you decide instead?
3.prayer:
Father, deliver us from greed, comparison and the fear of lack. Let our identity come from
Christ and never from what we own. Break every chain mammon has tried to put on us. Jesus,
be our only Master. In Jesus' name. Amen.

4.title: Week 4 Recap: THE MULTIPLICATION CODE
4.recap:
**THE MULTIPLICATION CODE — build it, grow it, send it ahead.** We were commissioned to
**occupy till He comes** — engage productively, not passively wait (Ep 20). We learned why
the third servant failed: **fear buries gifts** (Ep 21). We committed to **develop our
gifts**, because gifts grow through use and skill creates opportunity (Ep 22). We looked
outward to **solve a problem**, the way Joseph saw more than a crisis (Ep 23). We chose to
**multiply rather than consume everything** (Ep 24). And yesterday we learned to **invest for
eternity** — sending treasure ahead where it lasts.

Tomorrow: the Grand Finale.
4.reading:
Read **Luke 19:11–26** — the parable of the pounds, our second anchor passage.

*As you read, look for:* what the master actually rewarded. Not the size of the return — the
*faithfulness* of the servant. And notice the one thing he would not accept: a gift left
buried.
questions: What did you put to work this week that you had previously been sitting on?
Fear buried the third servant's pound. What is fear currently burying in you?
"Occupy till I come." What does productive waiting look like for a teenager this year?
4.prayer:
Father, we will not bury what You have given us. Help us develop every gift, solve real
problems and produce value that serves people and honours You. Teach us to invest today for
eternal reward — knowing the reward is Yours to give, and not our achievement to claim.
In Jesus' name. Amen.
4.declaration:
I will multiply what God gives me.
I will invest today for eternal rewards.

shorts.title: CRACK THE STEWARDSHIP CODE
shorts.hook: Everybody serves a master. The scary part? Most people never find out who theirs is until money asks them to choose.
shorts.scripture: “No servant can serve two masters… Ye cannot serve God and mammon.” — Luke 16:13
shorts.truth: Jesus never said having money is wrong — He said serving it is. A master is whatever controls your choices and commands your loyalty. So the first stewardship question isn’t “How much do I have?” It’s “Who rules my heart?” Money is like a powerful car with no driver: brilliant when it’s directed, destructive when it takes the wheel. Keep it in your hand and off the throne.
shorts.challenge: Answer three questions honestly: What do I believe money can do for me? What financial pressure controls my emotions? How can I make money serve God’s purpose?
shorts.quote: Money must stay in your hand, never on the throne of your heart.

shorts.title: THE OWNER
shorts.hook: Your name is on the phone. Your face unlocks it. So why isn’t it actually yours?
shorts.scripture: “The earth is the LORD’S, and the fulness thereof.” — Psalm 24:1
shorts.truth: Everything belongs to God — the land, the minerals, your health, your intelligence, every opportunity that made your stuff possible. Stewardship starts the moment you stop acting like an absolute owner. Think about how carefully you’d handle a friend’s expensive laptop for a week. Your time, abilities and possessions deserve more care than that, because they belong to God.
shorts.challenge: Make a list titled “What God Owns but Has Placed in My Hands.” Get at least seven items down — time, money, devices, skills, opportunities.
shorts.quote: God is not a participant in the economy. He is the Owner.

shorts.title: THE STEWARD
shorts.hook: A school prefect has real authority. But the prefect does not own the school. Guess what that makes you?
shorts.scripture: “There was a certain rich man, which had a steward.” — Luke 16:1
shorts.truth: A steward manages someone else’s resources according to the owner’s instructions. The man in Luke 16 had access, authority and opportunity — but he never had ownership. Access creates responsibility; it never removes accountability. And the top quality God looks for in a manager isn’t brains or popularity or money. It’s faithfulness — doing right consistently, even when nobody is watching.
shorts.challenge: Pick one resource from yesterday’s inventory and answer three questions: Why has God placed this in my hands? Who can it help? How can I manage it better?
shorts.quote: Access is not ownership. Having it doesn’t mean owning it.

shorts.title: THE SOURCE
shorts.hook: That side job. That allowance. That gift someone dropped on you. None of them are your Source — they’re just the pipe.
shorts.scripture: “It is he that giveth thee power to get wealth.” — Deuteronomy 8:18
shorts.truth: Money rarely falls from heaven. It arrives through work, skill, creativity, gifts and opportunity — but behind every honest channel is the God who gives life, health, intelligence, strength, favour and ideas. A job can end. A customer can leave. A gift gets spent. God remains. Remembering that keeps you peaceful when a channel changes, and humble enough never to say, “I did this all by myself.”
shorts.challenge: Write down three channels God currently provides through. Beside each one write: “God is my Source; this is only a channel.”
shorts.quote: Never worship the channel and forget the Source.

shorts.title: THE ASSIGNMENT
shorts.hook: Two teens, identical phones. One scrolls for hours. One learns editing, designs flyers and serves a church media team. Same device. Different assignment.
shorts.scripture: “Occupy till I come.” — Luke 19:13
shorts.truth: The master didn’t hand out money to be admired or displayed — he expected it used. Every resource God gives carries an assignment: to meet needs, build capacity, create value, bless people, advance His Kingdom. A phone can be a distraction or a classroom, a camera or a business tool. Pleasure isn’t automatically sinful — but purpose must lead pleasure.
shorts.challenge: Pick one resource you own and write three productive assignments it can fulfil.
shorts.quote: The object is the same. The assignment decides everything.

shorts.title: THE ACCOUNT
shorts.hook: No serious student waits for the examiner to walk in before starting to learn. So why do we manage our lives like the review is never coming?
shorts.scripture: “Give an account of thy stewardship.” — Luke 16:2
shorts.truth: Every steward eventually explains what was done with what was received. God sees how you use your time, your money, your abilities, your influence, the people around you — nothing entrusted to you is outside His concern. And knowing a review is coming changes how you live now: you plan better, waste less, obey faster, stay honest. It’s also personal. Friends, background and social media influence you, but you still answer for your own choices.
shorts.challenge: Review your last seven days — time, money, internet, talents, opportunities. Write one improvement beside each.
shorts.quote: I will manage today because I will report tomorrow.

shorts.title: THE OWNERSHIP COVENANT
shorts.hook: Five days, five answers. Who owns everything? Who are you? What must you do? Why were you given anything at all? And what happens at the end?
shorts.scripture: “All things come of thee, and of thine own have we given thee.” — 1 Chronicles 29:14
shorts.truth: God owns everything — the world, silver and gold, your abilities, your time, your life. He isn’t asking to become part-owner. You are the steward, and the better question isn’t “What do I have?” but “How am I managing what belongs to God?” Your life is an assignment, not an accident. And like a courier carrying a package that isn’t his, you’ll be measured by whether it reached the right destination — because one day you will give an account.
shorts.challenge: Build a Personal Resource Inventory — time, money, gifts, knowledge, devices, relationships, opportunities, influence — and write one way you’ll manage each more faithfully.
shorts.quote: God owns everything. I am only a steward. My life is an assignment.

shorts.title: FAITHFUL IN LITTLE
shorts.hook: "I'll be responsible when I have real money." Careful — a leaking bucket doesn't need more water. It needs the leak fixed.
shorts.scripture: "He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much." — Luke 16:10
shorts.truth: Your little is not meaningless. It is the test. A bigger allowance won't hand you discipline, wisdom or contentment — those get built before increase arrives. Small amounts are the training ground where you learn to record, save, give and wait. Don't despise the day of small things.
shorts.challenge: Name three small things you already manage. For each one, write the one habit that would prove you're faithful with it.
shorts.quote: My little is not useless. My little is my test.

shorts.title: KNOW WHAT YOU HAVE
shorts.hook: Your phone can tell you exactly which app drained your battery. Can you say the same about your money?
shorts.scripture: "Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds." — Proverbs 27:23
shorts.truth: You cannot manage accurately what you refuse to measure. The shepherd counted his flock — which were healthy, which were missing. You may feel like you don't spend much; written records tell the truth about repeated purchases and emotional spending. And money isn't the only flock. Time, screen hours and study hours all deserve the same attention.
shorts.challenge: For seven days, write down everything you receive and spend — date, amount, purpose, and whether it was a need or a want.
shorts.quote: I measure what I manage. I improve what I measure.

shorts.title: PLAN BEFORE YOU SPEND
shorts.hook: No football team runs onto the pitch with everyone chasing the ball wherever they feel like. They use a formation. So does your money.
shorts.scripture: "Which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost?" — Luke 14:28
shorts.truth: A budget is a plan that gives money an assignment before emotions spend it. Jesus praised the builder who counted the cost first — planning is not a lack of faith. Without a plan, the loudest desire takes everything. With one, giving, saving, spending, investing and learning each keep their place. A budget isn't punishment; it's permission to spend without regret.
shorts.challenge: Before your next allowance or side-job pay arrives, assign every part of it: give, save, spend, invest, learn.
shorts.quote: I will direct my money before it disappears.

shorts.title: FAITHFUL WITH ANOTHER PERSON’S
shorts.hook: Two students borrow cameras. One comes back clean, charged and packed. One comes back late, scratched, missing a cover. Who gets the better camera next time?
shorts.scripture: "If ye have not been faithful in that which is another man’s, who shall give you that which is your own?" — Luke 16:12
shorts.truth: How you treat what belongs to others reveals whether you're ready for your own. Borrowed things are a test: ask, handle carefully, return promptly, report damage honestly. Shared things count too — the chairs, books, computers and water that feel like they belong to nobody actually belong to a community. Trust is what opens doors.
shorts.challenge: Today, do one: return what you borrowed, repair what you damaged, replace what you lost, or clean a shared space.
shorts.quote: I honour God by caring for what belongs to another.

shorts.title: CHARACTER BEFORE CASH
shorts.hook: The cashier hands you too much change. Nobody noticed. Nobody will. What you do next is not about the money.
shorts.scripture: "If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?" — Luke 16:11
shorts.truth: Money tests character. It rarely creates greed, fear or dishonesty — it exposes what was already there, along with generosity and self-control. So never trade your character for extra change, exam malpractice, online fraud or a secret commission; money gained through corruption costs more than it pays. Jesus pointed to "true riches" — wisdom, integrity, trust — and those are handed only to the trustworthy.
shorts.challenge: Review your recent money moves and correct one dishonest thing — change, borrowing, a sale, a school payment, shared money.
shorts.quote: I will never exchange integrity for income.

shorts.title: THE FAITHFULNESS TEST
shorts.hook: Brushing your teeth for a whole hour once a month will not save them. This week we learned the same thing about money — five days, one test: consistency.
shorts.scripture: "He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much." — Luke 16:10
shorts.truth: Faithful in little. Know what you have. Plan before you spend. Protect what belongs to others. Character before cash. That's the week — and none of it works as one impressive action followed by weeks of carelessness. Faithfulness is right things done repeatedly, quietly, honestly, and it leans on simple systems: records, a budget, saving, accountability. The goal was never more money. It's greater trust, and a character ready for whatever God places in your hands.
shorts.challenge: Build your four-part Faithfulness System: what you'll record, what you'll save, what you'll stop wasting, and who will hold you accountable.
shorts.quote: Faithfulness is not one good action. It is a pattern.

shorts.title: TWO MASTERS
shorts.hook: Two people cannot turn the same steering wheel in opposite directions. So who is actually driving your money decisions?
shorts.scripture: “Ye cannot serve God and mammon.” — Luke 16:13
shorts.truth: A master has the right to command. If money is your master, it will tell you to chase it, compromise, compare and fear. Mammon isn’t just currency — it’s the security and identity people hand over to money. Jesus never offered a comfortable partnership. One must sit above the other: Christ is Master, you are His steward, money is your servant.
shorts.challenge: Finish this sentence honestly — “Money most often tries to control me through __________.” Then write one biblical response to that pressure.
shorts.quote: One wheel. One driver. One Master.

shorts.title: GOLD IS NOT MY GOD
shorts.hook: Most people quote this verse wrong. The Bible never says money is the root of all evil.
shorts.scripture: “For the love of money is the root of all evil.” — 1 Timothy 6:10
shorts.truth: It’s the love of money that does the damage — craving wealth above righteousness, measuring people by possessions, refusing contentment. Money makes a terrible god. It cannot forgive sin, give eternal life, guarantee peace or satisfy your soul. It can solve financial problems; it cannot carry the weight of worship. Fire in the cooker warms the house. Fire loose in the house destroys it.
shorts.challenge: List three things money can never give you. Then list three ways you can use money responsibly this week.
shorts.quote: Money can solve problems. It cannot carry worship.

shorts.title: POSSESSIONS MUST NOT POSSESS ME
shorts.hook: There’s a teenager who only feels confident wearing one particular brand of shoe. That shoe isn’t being worn anymore. It’s doing the wearing.
shorts.scripture: “And he was sad at that saying, and went away grieved: for he had great possessions.” — Mark 10:22
shorts.truth: The rich young ruler’s wealth wasn’t the whole problem. He could not release what stood between him and obeying Jesus. Phones, shoes, clothes, schools, your online image — all of it can be enjoyed, but none of it decides your worth. And you rarely know how attached you are until you’re asked to share it, delay it, or live without it. A steward can let go, because identity and security are already found in God.
shorts.challenge: Pick one possession you value highly and ask: Why do I value it? How would I feel without it? Could I release it if God required it?
shorts.quote: I possess things. Things do not possess me.

shorts.title: NEEDS, WANTS AND PRESSURE
shorts.hook: Your phone worked perfectly this morning. Then you saw your friend’s new one. Nothing broke — so what actually changed?
shorts.scripture: “I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.” — Philippians 4:11
shorts.truth: A need keeps you healthy, safe and responsible. A want is desirable but not essential — and a want isn’t wrong until you start calling it a need. Pressure is what blurs the line: friends, ads, influencers, trends, fear of missing out. It turns a useful desire into an emotional emergency. Notice Paul said, “I have learned.” Contentment isn’t giving up on growth. It’s being grateful and peaceful while you work responsibly for better.
shorts.challenge: Label every purchase you consider today: need, useful want, or pressure-driven want. Delay every pressure-driven one for at least seven days.
shorts.quote: Pressure turns a want into an emergency.

shorts.title: GIVE MONEY AN ASSIGNMENT
shorts.hook: A hammer never decides what it builds. Neither does your money. Somebody gives it direction — and if it isn’t you, it will be pressure.
shorts.scripture: “Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness.” — Luke 16:9
shorts.truth: Money is a tool, and tools take instructions from the hand holding them. Your allowance, your side job, your savings can be directed to feed, educate, build, support, create, give and solve. Income was never meant to stop at your own consumption — it should become impact. And generosity is what breaks the illusion that money must be held at all costs. Every time you give, your heart remembers: God is my Source. I am a steward, not an owner.
shorts.challenge: Today, use part of your money, time or skill to meet one genuine need. Do it quietly and on purpose.
shorts.quote: Untold money spends itself. Give yours an assignment.

shorts.title: BREAK MAMMON’S CHAINS
shorts.hook: A prisoner’s chain can be made of gold. It still holds him. That’s the week we just walked through — every chain money uses, and how each one breaks.
shorts.scripture: “Ye cannot serve God and mammon.” — Luke 16:13
shorts.truth: No servant serves two masters. Gold makes a poor god — it cannot forgive, heal or satisfy. Possessions must never own your confidence. Pressure must never rename your wants as needs. And money left without an assignment will quietly assign itself. Mammon chains through disobedience, through identity, and through fear — being afraid of not having enough, of losing what you hold, of being seen as poor. Wise planning is good; constant financial fear is bondage.
shorts.challenge: Practise one act of financial freedom today — give something, delay a purchase, reject peer pressure, or thank God for what you already have.
shorts.quote: A golden chain is still a chain.

shorts.title: OCCUPY UNTIL HE COMES
shorts.hook: Ten servants. Ten pounds. One instruction — and it wasn’t “sit still and wait.”
shorts.scripture: “And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.” — Luke 19:13
shorts.truth: Occupy means engage productively. Jesus expects His servants to be spiritually faithful and actually busy until He returns. Work isn’t just a way to receive money — it serves people, builds character and can honour God. And prayer belongs with action: pray for wisdom, plan carefully, learn diligently, work honestly. Waiting for Christ is never an excuse for laziness.
shorts.challenge: Spend at least thirty minutes today developing a productive skill. Actual practice, not scrolling about it.
shorts.quote: Prayer invites God’s wisdom. Work puts that wisdom into action.

shorts.title: DO NOT BURY IT
shorts.hook: One servant lost nothing. Not a single coin. And he still got it wrong.
shorts.scripture: “Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin.” — Luke 19:20
shorts.truth: He handed back exactly what he received. Nothing stolen — but nothing multiplied either. Playing safe becomes disobedience when God has told you to act. Fear of failure, criticism or comparison keeps a gift safe and completely unproductive. Gifts grow only through use: practise, learn, take correction, serve, repeat.
shorts.challenge: Pick one gift you’ve been neglecting. Practise it for thirty minutes, then show the result to someone you trust.
shorts.quote: A gift left in its case makes no music. Take it out.

shorts.title: DEVELOP YOUR GIFT
shorts.hook: The most talented player on the field isn’t always the best player by the end of the season. Why not?
shorts.scripture: “Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings.” — Proverbs 22:29
shorts.truth: Potential only means you could become good at something — it is not mastery. Natural ability becomes valuable through practice, study, feedback and correction. Diligence means careful, consistent effort: arrive prepared, practise the basics, fix mistakes, keep learning. Excellence is usually just small acts of diligence stacked up. Skill also creates room to serve — a developed gift is useful to people.
shorts.challenge: Write a seven-day plan for one skill: what you’ll practise, how long, what you’ll study, and who will give you honest feedback.
shorts.quote: Talent gives you a beginning. Diligence produces the growth.

shorts.title: SOLVE A PROBLEM
shorts.hook: Joseph walked into Pharaoh’s throne room as a prisoner. He walked out governing Egypt. What changed? He brought a solution.
shorts.scripture: “Forasmuch as God hath shewed thee all this, there is none so discreet and wise as thou art.” — Genesis 41:39
shorts.truth: Everyone in Egypt could see the coming famine. Joseph brought a plan, a system and a long-term strategy. Value is created when wisdom and skill meet a real problem. Look around you — someone is struggling with a school subject, a phone, a mess, a message they can’t write. A steward asks, “What can I do to help?” People normally exchange money for something they genuinely value, so don’t only ask how to make money.
shorts.challenge: List three problems around you. For each, name who it affects, what skill could help, and one small solution you can test.
shorts.quote: Don’t only ask how to make money. Ask what problem you can solve.

shorts.title: MULTIPLY, DON’T CONSUME EVERYTHING
shorts.hook: Two teenagers get the same holiday income. One month later, one has memories. The other has tools. Same start — different stewardship.
shorts.scripture: “Then came the first, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds.” — Luke 19:16
shorts.truth: Spending isn’t the enemy. You must spend on food, transport, school, responsibilities — and some appropriate enjoyment. The trouble starts when everything gets consumed and nothing is preserved. Saving hands resources to your future self. Investing puts resources into something that may produce future value — books, courses, skills, tools, small projects, always with learning, patience and wise guidance. This isn’t a trick for getting rich; it’s faithfulness with what God entrusted.
shorts.challenge: For your next income, allocate it before you spend: give, save, spend, invest, learn — setting the saving and investing portions aside first.
shorts.quote: I am a creator and a multiplier, not merely a consumer.

shorts.title: INVEST FOR ETERNITY
shorts.hook: All week we’ve been multiplying. Now the question that decides what it was all for: where does it go when you can’t take it with you?
shorts.scripture: “Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.” — Luke 16:9
shorts.truth: Occupy till He comes. Don’t bury the gift. Develop it with diligence. Use it to solve a real problem. Multiply instead of consuming everything. But here is where the week lands: money is temporary — it gets spent, lost, outdated, left behind. People are not. Invest in people through education, mentoring, encouragement, training, the gospel, and the greatest return won’t be measured in money at all. The highest purpose of multiplication was never personal accumulation. It’s eternal impact.
shorts.challenge: Write your Personal Multiplication Plan: one gift to develop, one problem to solve, one amount to save, one investment to study, one person to help, one Kingdom project to support.
shorts.quote: Temporary resources, eternal purposes. Send your treasure on ahead.

shorts.title: THE FAITHFUL STEWARD
shorts.hook: Thirty-one days ago we said there was a code to crack. Today — the three words the whole month was walking toward.
shorts.scripture: “Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things.” — Matthew 25:21
shorts.truth: The faithful steward knows three things. God owns everything — that produces humility. Faithfulness is active: records, plans, honesty, developed gifts, problems solved, resources invested. And the greatest test was never the size of your account — it was whether Jesus Christ stayed your Master. Wealth may pass through your hands; it must never sit on the throne of your heart.
shorts.challenge: Write and sign the Stewardship Covenant. One habit you’ll begin, one waste you’ll stop, one skill you’ll develop, one cause you’ll support.
shorts.quote: The treasure may pass through the servant’s hands — but he is not the king.
